clean_body: The biggest National Memorial Day Parade yet Help send two Iwo Jima heroes to Arlington to honor their fallen brothers. | | | | | | | Friend, In 1944, a young Marine boarded a military transport plane, the first flight he'd ever taken.82 years later, he'll board his first commercial flight to honor his fallen World War II comrades during Memorial Day weekend. Billy Byrd served in the United States Marine Corps and was in the first wave that landed on Iwo Jima in February 1945. He fought for 32 straight days alongside the men of the legendary 28th Marines Regiment, 5th Marine Division.Billy was there when Mount Suribachi was taken, and he watched the American flag go up.One of the men raising that flag was his best friend, Ira Hayes. | | | | | | | | Above: Ira Hayes, one of the heroes who raised the American Flag at Iwo Jima. Friend, Billy has NOT stepped foot on an airplane since that military flight in 1944. Not once - until now.This month, at nearly 100 years old, Billy Byrd will take his FIRST-EVER commercial flight to Washington, D.C. To honor the men he fought beside... to visit Arlington National Cemetery for the first time... and to stand at the grave of his best friend, Ira Hayes, for the first time.Friend, will you help make this historic trip possible for Billy so he can honor his fallen World War II comrades? For more than 25 years, the American Veterans Center has worked to preserve the stories, sacrifice, and patriotism of America's veterans - like Billy Byrd - before those stories are lost forever. Through national events like the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C., nationwide educational programs, documentaries, and our historic oral history archives......AVC has helped millions of Americans hear directly from the heroes who defended our freedom -- from World War II and Korea to Vietnam, Iraq, and Afghanistan. Every year since 2005, AVC has brought together veterans, Gold Star families, active-duty troops, and patriotic Americans during Memorial Day weekend to honor the men and women who served this country with courage and made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedom.We believe America 's veterans are not just part of our history... they ARE the guardians of our freedom. And as America approaches her 250th birthday, that mission matters more than ever.Friend, when you support the American Veterans Center, you are helping ensure that heroes like Billy Byrd and Don Graves and their fallen brothers-in-arms are honored, remembered, and celebrated by future generations of Americans. Friend, your support will also help Billy reunite with fellow Iwo Jima Marine veteran Don Graves.These two Marines became brothers during one of the bloodiest battles in American history.And the American Veterans Center is bringing them back together in less than ten days at this year 's National Memorial Day Parade. Above: Don Graves (L) and Billy Byrd (R) Friend, Don Graves has his own incredible story.He was barely 17 years old when he heard President Roosevelt's speech after Pearl Harbor and joined the Marines. On Iwo Jima, Don carried a 72-pound flamethrower onto the beach under enemy fire. Don's platoon was also assigned to take Mount Suribachi.He fought day and night against relentless Japanese attacks. And last year, at nearly 100 years old, Don became the OLDEST man in history to sign a recording contract in Nashville.He even sang "God Bless America" at last year's parade. Friend, these are the men who saved the world and kept America free from tyranny - the men who defended the same liberty first won by our Founders 250 years ago.This year, as America celebrates her 250th birthday, we remember that freedom survives because brave men step forward in every generation. In 1776, patriots pledged their lives, fortunes, and sacred honor.In 1945, Billy Byrd, Don Graves, Ira Hayes, and countless others carried that same spirit onto the black sands of Iwo Jima.Friend, men like Billy and Don ARE America. Their courage, sacrifice, and love of country embody the spirit of 1776.And right now, the American Veterans Center needs your help to honor them properly. We are covering Billy and Don's travel to Washington... Their transportation...Their meals...And arranging their visit to Arlington National Cemetery so Billy can stand beside Ira Hayes one final time.But we cannot do it without grassroots patriots like YOU. We have ten days to get Billy and Don to Washington - please rush your gift today if you can. | | | | | | | | Above: Photos of the U.S. Marines in action on Iwo Jima featured in Billy's autobiography, By the Dawn's Early Light: From the Cottonfields of Mississippi to the Beaches of Iwo Jima. Extremist Republicans are finalizing a plan to redraw Alabama’s map beyond recognition, breaking up my district so Republican seats can absorb it and silence the voices of the people I was elected to represent.

Right now Republicans are targeting the voting power of Black people in Alabama – who make up nearly one-third of the population. They are the ones getting their representation, their voice, and their power stripped away from them.
It’s a blatant power grab by the GOP, and they're dangerously close to getting away with it. If we don’t fight back now, the damage could last for decades to come. And as Democrats, we'd be foolish to think their gerrymandering scheme wouldn't spread like wildfire beyond the South.
I'm doing everything I can to stop this, but fights like this take resources, courage, and a grassroots army behind me. We need to get people educated, registered and motivated to get out to vote, despite having the odds stacked against us.

Hantavirus and Ebola outbreaks could be worse than COVID.
In 2020, health "experts" engineered a ridiculous lockdown in response to COVID so they could sabotage the economy and the Presidential election, and it looks like Democrats may be dusting off the old playbook with Ebola and the Hantavirus.
Today, the CDC and World Health Organization are gravely concerned about an Ebola outbreak in the Congo, which has infected one [American](https://substack.com/redirect/c438ba1a-34d2-4547-a412-4ea62939875c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the region and hundreds of others. CDC is limiting U.S. travel for individuals originating from the Congo. No one in the United States has been confirmed to have Ebola, and with a mortality rate of 25-50%, let's hope that holds. But Ebola isn't the only virus running rampant today.
The hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius is being presented to the American people as a contained public health incident with "extremely low" risk to the general public, but we may not be getting the whole truth.

After COVID, the American people are rightly suspicious of public health officials. They failed us then, and they may be failing us now.
Although Anthony Fauci is long gone, the same Fauci-era institutions, the same virology bureaucracy, and the same public health apparatus that botched, politicized, and weaponized the COVID response are still in power. The consequences for Americans could be disastrous.
The CDC[ confirmed](https://substack.com/redirect/59b4a5a5-e3af-4202-b6bc-0f9bb112eac3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it is responding to a deadly outbreak of Andes virus, a type of hantavirus, among passengers and crew on the MV Hondius, a cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean. The agency says the risk of a pandemic and the overall risk to the American public remain extremely low. CDC also says Andes virus is not new, is normally found in parts of South America, and is the only type of hantavirus known to spread person to person, though that spread is usually limited to close contact with symptomatic individuals.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2da52d55-f72a-40d1-a66d-dfa1ad72602e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

According to CDC's own Health Alert Network advisory, the World Health Organization was notified on May 2, 2026, of a cluster of severe acute respiratory illness among passengers and crew aboard the ship. By May 8, WHO had reported eight cases, including six confirmed cases, two suspected cases, and three deaths. The ship carried 147 people from 23 countries and traveled through remote locations after departing Ushuaia, Argentina.
Then, HHS announced that, through ASPR and CDC, it was supporting the State Department in repatriating American citizens from the affected ship to specialized care facilities in the United States, including the University of Nebraska Medical Center/Nebraska Medicine in Omaha. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said the department had deployed the nation's leading medical and public health resources.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c0ec1bb3-aca4-420a-9084-1d0c5eaf67f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

We were gaslit that calling COVID a [Chinese virus was racist](https://substack.com/redirect/b9f134ab-bacf-4587-b5a5-111e2f666502?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

| | May 21, 2026

**Westfield, IN -** Today, Congresswoman Victoria Spartz issued the following statement:

"I started over 20 years ago in the conservative grassroots of Republican politics in the state of Indiana with so many fighters for this Republic and true patriots, many of whom are no longer with us. And I know, on this 250th anniversary of our Republic, that we are facing a huge battle this November for the future of this nation — one we cannot afford to lose. I urge all of my fellow conservatives, libertarians, constitutionalists, fiscal hawks, and moderates within the Republican Party — and especially all of our convention delegates — to support Max Engling as our next nominee for Secretary of State. Max is a family man, a fighter, and someone who will work hard to help us defeat the radical left. I urge the other nominees to withdraw their nominations and unite in support of Max. Max Engling has my complete and total endorsement to be our next Indiana Secretary of State."

body:
This is how we build a party that invests in our communities and wins in more places.
#
Peter,
I know a lot of campaigns are asking for money, so I want to be clear about what your donation to Small Town PAC actually helps build.
It helps us build the infrastructure to compete in communities too many politicians have written off — _not just in the final weeks of an election, but early enough to matter._
It helps us get on the road, meet people where they are, and lift up leaders who understand the places they want to represent.
Leaders who know a local school is not just a building — it is where neighbors come together after football games, graduations, concerts, and tough days when someone needs help.
Leaders who will fight for the basic things every community deserves: strong schools, good jobs, health care close to home, child care families can afford, and a real voice in our politics.
**That is how Democrats start competing in more places again: by showing up early, investing in communities that have been ignored, and backing people who know how to fight for them.**
[**Can you make a contribution of $5 or whatever makes sense for you today to help Small Town PAC build the grassroots power Democrats need to expand the map?**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260521-1.PKGR0Z&amount=5&refcode=em20260521-667&t=1&akid=667%2E34582%2E69JLQc)
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260521-1.PKGR0Z&amount=5&refcode=20260521-667&t=20&akid=667%2E34582%2E69JLQc)**
The other side has billionaires, tech bros, venture capitalists, and robber barons trying to buy our elections and rip our communities apart.
We have people chipping in what they can because they believe our communities deserve better. That may not sound flashy. _But it is how you build something real._
A few dollars at a time. A few more organizers. A few more candidates. A few more places where Democrats can start showing up again.
That is how we build a party that invests in our communities, delivers a message that actually resonates, and wins elections in places too many people have given up on.
[**Please make a contribution to Small Town PAC today. Every dollar helps us build this movement and put power back into the hands of our neighbors.**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260521-1.PKGR0Z&amount=5&refcode=em20260521-667&t=21&akid=667%2E34582%2E69JLQc)
I’m grateful you’re part of this.
Tim

Tim Walz started Small Town PAC to build a Democratic Party that invests in small towns and delivers a message that resonates with rural America.
Together, we're finding and recruiting thoughtful, hardworking people to run for office, and supporting a new generation of leaders who truly reflect and understand their communities.
**[It’s time for Democrats to expand the map and put small towns back at the forefront: pitch in now to help build our movement from the ground up.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/stp-ms-em-footer?refcode=em20260521-667&t=22&refcode2=667_34582_69JLQc&akid=667%2E34582%2E69JLQc)**

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way we keep in touch with people like you, so thank you for reading to the end.

Hey folks,
This one went everywhere -- and honestly, I think that's why people keep showing up.
**Jack Cocchiarella** and I started by yelling about Jared Polis, Trump stooges, and billionaire tax scams... and somehow ended up in a brutally honest conversation about loneliness, young men, dating apps, schools, social media, and what happens when an entire generation grows up without real role models.
We got personal in this one. Frustrated. Vulnerable. Hopeful, too. I think a lot of you are going to see yourselves somewhere in this conversation.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:04:20**] Jack unloads on Jared Polis after the Colorado governor's controversial clemency decision -- and why Democrats are finally demanding accountability from their own.
* [**00:17:03**] We break down the difference between compromising with Trump and completely surrendering your values -- plus why Bernie still connects with people in ways other Democrats don't.
* [**00:27:21**] Jeff Bezos says teachers shouldn't pay taxes. We explain why billionaire propaganda is getting more dangerous -- and how the ultra-wealthy are trying to rewrite the social contract in real time.
* [**00:36:23**] The conversation shifts hard into isolation, dating apps, technology, and why so many people -- especially young men -- feel disconnected, angry, and lost.
* [**00:51:13**] We close with a difficult but important conversation about masculinity, role models, education, and why Democrats cannot afford to ignore what's happening to young men online.

This episode covers politics, culture, technology, masculinity, loneliness, class, and the growing sense that too many people are drifting through life without connection or purpose. **DEL. RASOUL STATEMENT ON COLLECTIVE BARGAINING VETO** When I first began in politics, a union hall was a bastion of Democratic politics. Now, going into union meetings, many in the crowd have been persuaded by right-wing social and identity politics. That's because in the 1980s, the Democratic Party began to abandon our middle-class roots and chase corporate money. I am disappointed in Gov. Spanberger's veto of collective bargaining, but not surprised. When half of Democratic leadership can rationalize bombing kids in schools abroad, costing a billion dollars a day, but can't guarantee school supplies for our teachers, it's no wonder why people lose hope in our party. Demand more from me and from us when it comes to the kitchen table basics. The 2026 Midterm, 2027 VA GA, and the 2028 Presidential elections must be a turning point for us to be sure that those at the very top hear our voices loud and clear.

* 372,000 inactive voters removed from rolls in Colorado

* Settlement to remove 800,000 ineligible voters in Oregon

* A BRAND NEW lawsuit against California to clean up 873,000 inactive voters

Leftist groups and their political operatives are in the courts pushing harder than ever to eliminate election integrity safeguards needed to ensure fair and honest elections. To fund their efforts, _they are rolling in money from the Soros network_ , and reviving election law schemes from the Biden-Harris years that have radical goals like:

Peter, we know what Trump’s agenda includes: skyrocketing prices, families struggling to afford rent and groceries, workers having to choose between their careers or caring for their loved ones.
**Now, Trump is trying to bring that same agenda to California through his endorsed candidate, Steve Hilton.**
That’s why this race matters so much, Peter: _the governor is the last line of defense against Trump._ If he gets a foothold here, Californians will pay the price.
**[If that’s all you need to hear, rush a $5 contribution to power Katie’s campaign through the June 2nd primary.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260521_1_ak.yOigz0&refcode=em20260521-41394&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=41394%2E3422442%2EOmqdGz)**

**Katie refuses to let Trump drag this state backward.**
She’s spent her career taking him on, exposing his abuses of power, and holding his allies accountable when they stack the system against working families.
As governor, she’ll keep fighting back— _no corporate loopholes, no billionaire handouts, no MAGA agenda sneaking into California._
While Trump and his MAGA allies slash health care, Katie is fighting for single-payer health care so Californians can actually afford the care they need.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131834932/622468652/701031031?refcode=em-5.21.26-all-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDhmMDYzOTktMzE1NS1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTg5MDVjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=xilKDFaGCugZUIJJoF-ZzFV6JNutHANkv4u1ZnNmeaY=) Peter, it's Senator Bernie Sanders.

Let me start with something most of us instinctively know to be true.

And that is that running as a progressive in this country is never easy. You are often taking on the corporate establishment, the media establishment, and sometimes even your own party's political establishment.

But as progressives, we also understand something that most in the Democratic Establishment does not:

And that is that while it is essential that we defeat Trumpism and all its ugly and destructive policies, we need to do more. We need to elect candidates who have the guts to stand up to the wealthiest people on earth, not simply beg those people for money.

No more tinkering around the edges. No more status quo politics.

In the United States every man, woman and child can and must enjoy a decent standard of living. That’s what the American people want, and that’s what we have to deliver.

This month, the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee announced they are backing Randy Villegas' Democratic primary opponent. It is disappointing, but it is not surprising.

But as we have seen time and time again, from Maine to California, the backing of establishment Democrats is no match for when working class people stand up and get involved to elect candidates who will work to create a government and an economy that works for ALL, not just the 1%.

**Randy Villegas is one of those candidates. And with ballots already in the mail, I am once again asking for your financial support:**

body:
| Hey team! It’s Kalliana jumping in quickly because I wanted to make sure you saw Sue’s email earlier (I forwarded it below, too). She shared a little behind-the-scenes look at some recent campaign stops across Rhode Island — house parties, conversations with voters, radio interviews, all the fun “campaign on the road” stuff. But there were also two really important asks in there:
---
| |
* Sue wants to hear directly from you: if you were sitting with her at one of these events, what would you ask her about the race for Lieutenant Governor? **[You can ask here!](https://sue4ri.com/l/9NyePeyafUhc)**

| | [ **SUBMIT YOUR QUESTION** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/r22CHvZJ1oWQ)
---
* And if you’re able, helping fund more travel/events/organizing across the state would mean a lot right now. **[I’d love to be able to tell Sue that this email helped raise those funds that we need right now!](https://sue4ri.com/l/g8RYFpvQboUx)**

| [ **DONATE** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/MTXsycoZ2zNy)
---
This campaign has such good energy right now because people are genuinely engaging and showing up. We’re really excited about what’s being built here. Thanks for being part of it, Kalliana
---
**Begin forwarded message:**
> ****
> Hi friend —
>
> One of my favorite parts of this campaign has been getting out across Rhode Island and having real conversations with people face-to-face.
>
> I’m not talking about official speaking engagements or political theater. These events are just people gathering in living rooms, community centers, coffee shops, radio studios, and anywhere there’s space to talk honestly about what Rhode Islanders need from their government right now — and what the Lieutenant Governor’s office could be if we expected more from it.
>
> _And if you have thoughts on that —**[I want to hear them, share here!](https://sue4ri.com/l/Lmzng2s593Ly)**_
>
> So I wanted to bring a little bit of that “on the road” energy directly to you today. (Plus, if you’re anything like me, you get how big of a deal it is to get folks to travel anywhere in this state — I’m so grateful!)
> **⬇️ Here are a few recent stops from the campaign trail ⬇️**
> | |
> **📍 Cranston**
>
> I had such a great conversation with the folks at this gathering about the kind of new energy we can bring to the Lieutenant Governor’s office. They had thoughtful questions about affordability, climate resilience, how we fight fascism with community, and what it actually looks like when government listens before it acts.
>
> Honestly, one of the biggest themes of the night was this feeling that people are ready for leadership that feels more accessible, collaborative, and that actually takes responsibility. They are ready for an LG who wants to roll her sleeves up and get something done. That’s me!
> * * *
> **📍 Woonsocket**
>
> I stopped by Coalition Radio in Woonsocket to chat with Pat Ford about something I care about deeply: how government can actually work with people to get things done.
>
> We talked about energy policy, traffic safety, collaboration, and what it means to build a government that’s responsive instead of reactive. These are exactly the kinds of conversations shaping this campaign every single day. Did you hear it? **[If not, you can find the recording here>>](https://sue4ri.com/l/5b6AKA622L1E)**
> * * *
> **📍 Providence**
>
> This (beautiful!) stop at Mare in Wayland Square, Providence, left me feeling genuinely hopeful about Rhode Island’s future. We talked about housing, affordability, climate, and what people want to see from their leaders right now.
>
> But more than anything, I left inspired by how engaged and thoughtful everyone was. These conversations remind me why I’m running in the first place.
>
> ---
>
>
> Honestly? I wish every single one of you could pull up a chair at one of these events. So let me ask:
>
>
> 💬 **[If you were sitting with me at one of these house parties, what question would you want to ask me about this race or my vision for Lieutenant Governor?](https://sue4ri.com/l/aYNyM7lHeqhF)**
> | [ **SUBMIT YOUR QUESTION** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/sdFBRliX3y29)
> ---
> And if you want to help us keep this kind of organizing going — more stops, more conversations, more community events across Rhode Island — **[you can chip in here, too:](https://sue4ri.com/l/qSWyIfUVDyOr)**
> | [ **DONATE** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/iglCjor5aKkl)
> ---
> This campaign is growing because people are showing up for it. I’m grateful you’re here.
>
> More soon from the road,
>
> Sue
---
| Join Sue's journey to build a government that isn’t afraid to take on big challenges, that has your back, and will take responsibility for fixing things that are broken.

[ ****](https://sue4ri.com/l/mRH2SmwnQ0YE)**[Donate today to support a candidate who will have a major impact for good in Rhode Island.](https://sue4ri.com/l/VrS1FIJPypnD)**
---
[ DONATE ](https://sue4ri.com/l/yWYcIBy0yt7T)
---
| Paid for by Friends of AnderBois
---

name: Caitlin Cattelino
subject: Special Invitation: Write letters to protect the Arctic Refuge
body:
Join Defenders to learn more about the threats to the Arctic Refuge and how letters to the editors can make a difference!

Join Defenders to learn more about the threats to the Arctic Refuge and how letters to the editors can make a difference!
                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5536668/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5536669/38SyG9Xl)

Dear Defender,

The Arctic National Wildlife Refuge is the crown jewel of our refuge system and home to threatened polar bears, iconic caribou and hundreds of species of migratory birds. Unfortunately, the Trump administration is proposing to expand oil and gas drilling in the Arctic Refuge. This reckless attempt at more unnecessary development could cause irreparable damage to the wildlife and communities who depend on its vast landscape.

Wildlife Defenders, like you, have the power to speak up and change things for the better! Join us for a workshop via Zoom (https://support.defenders.org/s/5536670/38SyG9Xl) to learn how you can write powerful letters to the editor that oppose destructive oil and gas development in the Arctic Refuge!

Here are the details:

What: Wildlife Defenders’ Briefing Webinar:

Defend the Arctic Refuge

When: Thursday, May 28

Time: 7:00pmET / 6:00pmCT / 5:00pmMT / 4:00pmPT

Register here – a zoom link will be sent to you (https://support.defenders.org/s/5536671/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5536672/38SyG9Xl)

The Bureau of Land Management is currently accepting bids for oil and gas leases on Alaska’s Coastal Plain. The Coastal Plain is the biological heart of the Arctic Refuge – a vital landscape that sustains avian wildlife whose migrations connect all 50 states and six continents. It is the most important onshore maternal denning habitat for polar bears in the United States and where the Porcupine Caribou Herd migrates to annually to give birth.

One of the biggest ways you can help is by writing letters to the editor to local newspapers and other publications. Your letter will bring attention to the serious threat facing the Arctic Refuge and help deliver the message to oil and gas companies that drilling in the refuge is destructive, risky and not welcome!

We’re excited to have you join us as we work to protect the Arctic Refuge. Thank you for speaking up and making the world a better place for the people and wildlife who call it home.

Hope to see you soon! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5536673/38SyG9Xl)

Caitlin Cattelino

Director of National Outreach

Defenders of Wildlife

(http://www.facebook.com/DefendersofWildlife) (http://twitter.com/defenders) (https://www.instagram.com/defendersofwildlife/?hl=en) (http://www.youtube.com/defendersofwildlife) (https://www.tiktok.com/@defendersofwildlife)

Defenders of Wildlife 1130 17th Street NW • Washington, DC 20036 defenders.org (https://defenders.org)

Billy Byrd served in the United States Marine Corps and was in the first wave that landed on Iwo Jima in February 1945. clean_body: They saw the flag raised over Iwo Jima Help send two Iwo Jima heroes to Arlington to honor their fallen brothers. | | | | | | | Peter, In 1944, a young Marine boarded a military transport plane, the first flight he'd ever taken.82 years later, he'll board his first commercial flight to honor his fallen World War II comrades during Memorial Day weekend. Billy Byrd served in the United States Marine Corps and was in the first wave that landed on Iwo Jima in February 1945. He fought for 32 straight days alongside the men of the legendary 28th Marines Regiment, 5th Marine Division.Billy was there when Mount Suribachi was taken, and he watched the American flag go up.One of the men raising that flag was his best friend, Ira Hayes. | | | | | | | | Above: Ira Hayes, one of the heroes who raised the American Flag at Iwo Jima. Peter, Billy has NOT stepped foot on an airplane since that military flight in 1944. Not once - until now.This month, at nearly 100 years old, Billy Byrd will take his FIRST-EVER commercial flight to Washington, D.C. To honor the men he fought beside... to visit Arlington National Cemetery for the first time... and to stand at the grave of his best friend, Ira Hayes, for the first time.Peter, will you help make this historic trip possible for Billy so he can honor his fallen World War II comrades? For more than 25 years, the American Veterans Center has worked to preserve the stories, sacrifice, and patriotism of America's veterans - like Billy Byrd - before those stories are lost forever. Through national events like the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C., nationwide educational programs, documentaries, and our historic oral history archives......AVC has helped millions of Americans hear directly from the heroes who defended our freedom -- from World War II and Korea to Vietnam, Iraq, and Afghanistan. Every year since 2005, AVC has brought together veterans, Gold Star families, active-duty troops, and patriotic Americans during Memorial Day weekend to honor the men and women who served this country with courage and made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedom.We believe America 's veterans are not just part of our history... they ARE the guardians of our freedom. And as America approaches her 250th birthday, that mission matters more than ever.Peter, when you support the American Veterans Center, you are helping ensure that heroes like Billy Byrd and Don Graves and their fallen brothers-in-arms are honored, remembered, and celebrated by future generations of Americans. Peter, your support will also help Billy reunite with fellow Iwo Jima Marine veteran Don Graves.These two Marines became brothers during one of the bloodiest battles in American history.And the American Veterans Center is bringing them back together in less than ten days at this year 's National Memorial Day Parade. Above: Don Graves (L) and Billy Byrd (R) Peter, Don Graves has his own incredible story.He was barely 17 years old when he heard President Roosevelt's speech after Pearl Harbor and joined the Marines. On Iwo Jima, Don carried a 72-pound flamethrower onto the beach under enemy fire. Don's platoon was also assigned to take Mount Suribachi.He fought day and night against relentless Japanese attacks. And last year, at nearly 100 years old, Don became the OLDEST man in history to sign a recording contract in Nashville.He even sang "God Bless America" at last year's parade. Peter, these are the men who saved the world and kept America free from tyranny - the men who defended the same liberty first won by our Founders 250 years ago.This year, as America celebrates her 250th birthday, we remember that freedom survives because brave men step forward in every generation. In 1776, patriots pledged their lives, fortunes, and sacred honor.In 1945, Billy Byrd, Don Graves, Ira Hayes, and countless others carried that same spirit onto the black sands of Iwo Jima.Peter, men like Billy and Don ARE America. Their courage, sacrifice, and love of country embody the spirit of 1776.And right now, the American Veterans Center needs your help to honor them properly. We are covering Billy and Don's travel to Washington... Their transportation...Their meals...And arranging their visit to Arlington National Cemetery so Billy can stand beside Ira Hayes one final time.But we cannot do it without grassroots patriots like YOU. We have ten days to get Billy and Don to Washington - please rush your gift today if you can. | | | | | | | | Above: Photos of the U.S. Marines in action on Iwo Jima featured in Billy's autobiography, By the Dawn's Early Light: From the Cottonfields of Mississippi to the Beaches of Iwo Jima. Midterms: Common Sense Verses Crazy/ Chaos
---
Americans want to live, work, and raise our families in peace. But dangerous Democrats in Washington and Richmond are still pushing ludicrous ideas like open borders, soft on crime polices that put dangerous criminals back on our streets, high taxes, and boys in girls sports. Clearly, this years midterms will be about common sense verse crazy and common sense verse chaos. We need all hands on deck. We need you to help us get out the vote so we can stop the woke anti-American non-sense.
To help our campaign to save Virginia's 5th District go to [www.mcguireva.com](https://eky6fg9ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001aBzILgIl_DyYPBMwkKiVUK3NDBTfu5F2B7C-Ls2EzGJYyk8Tk1meXisHR8Di4OPMG00IXepzRnSEXwRr-FrLKUzhEdtis-fpkQ5taAxcPX4mB_BU_Ahem0P-c6N-MStoSUbHfJcadBqGYK7nGMVJfJw8TLwwopn7&c=-9ldd6UHMuNigrn2AixomiSG_eEDhiQeA62R9U6KHDh--20m6O-VuA==&ch=JGuCbvsiq4Brhh4sZXndmtkbePzJ7-zAhUyxAZvXuEEvOoZ0kKrEhw==)

* PROTECT Kids Act (H.R. 2616)
* Lulu's Law (S. 1003).

---
Endorsement From Our Commander In Chief President Trump
---
| | | |
---

"Congressman John McGuire is an America First Warrior for Virginia's 5th Congressional District. John bravely served our Great Country as a U.S. Navy SEAL, and is doing an incredible job fighting for the people of Rural Virginia. He is working hard to Grow our Economy, Create GREAT Jobs, Champion American Energy DOMINANCE, Secure our Border, Strengthen our Military/Veterans, Defend our always under siege Second Amendment, and Restore PEACE THROUGH STRENGTH. John is MAGA all the way, and has been with us from the very beginning. John McGuire has my Complete and Total Endorsement - He will never let you down!"\- President Donald Trump
Riley Gaines Endorsement
---
|
---
It is an honor to be endorsed by such an incredible champion for women's sports, and the conservative movement. I've enjoyed working with Riley through the years and most recently on my Riley Gaines Act. Thank you for the endorsement, and everything you do to protect women's spaces. "I am proud to endorse Congressman John McGuire for re-election. I first worked with John to protect women in sports when he served in the Virginia General Assembly, and he has continued that fight in Congress. He authored the Riley Gaines Act to safeguard female athletes and defend Title IX. As a former Navy SEAL, John brings real courage and common sense to this battle for fairness and truth. Virginia families can trust him to do what's right. I urge you to support Congressman John McGuire." Riley Gaines 12-time NCAA All-American & SEC Champion Host of The Riley Gaines Show Advocate for women's sports & fairness

| I ran into some amazing supporters from Mecklenburg County in Amherst County. They were headed to D.C. on Sunday for the National Jubilee of Prayer, Praise, and Thanksgiving, also known as Rededicate 250.

| Waving Good Morning
---
| |

| I hope you all had a wonderful Mother's Day weekend with your family. Before heading to D.C., I stopped by Lynchburg to wave hello to commuters on their way to work. It's a good thing Navy SEAL's are waterproof because we had Frogman weather that morning!
---
| Police Week Honoring Our Brave Men And Women
---

---
| We would not have a country without our brave men and women in law enforcement. This National Police Week, we remembered and honored the heroes who gave their lives to protect our communities.

| I am proud to be endorsed by 60 Plus - The American Association of Senior Citizens, as a Guardian of Seniors' Rights. We must take care of our seniors!

subject: Celebrating AANHPI Heritage Month
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Emerge America
body:
https://emergeamerica.org/ [https://emergeamerica.org/]
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVEMR/1/81321/images/Celebrating%20AANHPI%20Month%20%282026%29.png]
AANHPI Month is a time to celebrate the rich cultures, histories, and contributions of Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander communities across the country. It is also an important reminder that these communities are not a monolith - encompassing people with roots in dozens of countries, cultures, languages, and lived experiences.
Today, more than 25 million people in the United States identify as AANHPI. Over the last decade alone, the Asian American population grew by nearly 40%, while the Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander population grew by almost 30%. As these communities continue to grow, representation at every level of leadership matters more than ever.
That representation is already making a difference through Emerge alums who are stepping up to lead, advocate, and serve their communities.
In Virginia, Irene Shin has become a powerful voice for working families, reproductive freedom, and equitable policy solutions. In California, Helen Tran made history as the first Asian American elected mayor of San Bernardino, bringing lived experience and community-centered leadership to city hall.
Maryland Delegate Lily Qi has continued to champion immigrant communities, education, and economic opportunity while breaking barriers as one of the first Chinese American women elected to the Maryland General Assembly. And in Connecticut, Representative Maryam Khan fights for access to quality education, funding community infrastructure, and inclusion in decision-making, as the first Muslim member of the Connecticut House.
As AANHPI communities continue to grow across the country, so too must opportunities for leadership, visibility, and representation. Because when our leadership reflects the full diversity of America, our democracy becomes stronger for everyone.
- Cecilia Yoon
Manager for Grassroots and Development Support, Emerge

clean_body: [] [] AANHPI Month is a time to celebrate the rich cultures, histories, and contributions of Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander communities across the country. It is also an important reminder that these communities are not a monolith - encompassing people with roots in dozens of countries, cultures, languages, and lived experiences. Today, more than 25 million people in the United States identify as AANHPI. Over the last decade alone, the Asian American population grew by nearly 40%, while the Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander population grew by almost 30%. As these communities continue to grow, representation at every level of leadership matters more than ever. That representation is already making a difference through Emerge alums who are stepping up to lead, advocate, and serve their communities. In Virginia, Irene Shin has become a powerful voice for working families, reproductive freedom, and equitable policy solutions. In California, Helen Tran made history as the first Asian American elected mayor of San Bernardino, bringing lived experience and community-centered leadership to city hall. Maryland Delegate Lily Qi has continued to champion immigrant communities, education, and economic opportunity while breaking barriers as one of the first Chinese American women elected to the Maryland General Assembly. And in Connecticut, Representative Maryam Khan fights for access to quality education, funding community infrastructure, and inclusion in decision-making, as the first Muslim member of the Connecticut House. As AANHPI communities continue to grow across the country, so too must opportunities for leadership, visibility, and representation. Because when our leadership reflects the full diversity of America, our democracy becomes stronger for everyone. - Cecilia Yoon Manager for Grassroots and Development Support, Emerge Support Emerge Today [] secure.actblue.com/donate/emerge-2026-email?refcode=5-21 [secure.actblue.com/donate/emerge-2026-email?refcode=5-21] Paid for by Emerge America Emerge America 1301 K St NW Suite 300W Washington, D.C. 20005 CONTRIBUTE TODAY [] CONTRIBUTE MONTHLY []

name: Justin J. Pearson
subject: The most troubling abuses of power
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Last week, I received official notice from Tennessee House Speaker Cameron
Sexton that I had been removed from all of my state House committee
assignments — alongside every other Tennessee House Democrat.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260521-jp.dTBcvO&refcode=em20260521-37802&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1002&akid=37802%2E1203867%2EdAsVL5 ]Tweet from @Justinjpearson: 'Speaker of the TN House Cameron Sexton
just removed me and every Democrat — and therefore every Black elected
official in the state legislature from any committee we served on. This
move strips nearly 2 million Tennesseeans from the representation they
deserve in TN state leg.'

This is one of the most troubling abuses of power in our state’s history.

Peter, this
kind of retaliation only works if we let them intimidate us into silence.
I won’t let it, but I’ll need your help to keep fighting. [ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260521-jp.dTBcvO&refcode=em20260521-37802&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1003&akid=37802%2E1203867%2EdAsVL5 ]So if you’re
able to, split $10 or more right now with our campaign and Justice
Democrats to keep our grassroots Movement strong enough to defend
ourselves and our communities from this authoritarian attack.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260521-jp.dTBcvO&refcode=em20260521-37802&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1004&akid=37802%2E1203867%2EdAsVL5 ]Contribute $10 ››

If this sounds familiar, it should. Because this is what TN House
Republicans do when they don’t like what you have to say.

More than three years ago, they expelled me after I protested on the House
floor against their inaction on gun violence. They thought they could make
an example of me for refusing to be quiet while our communities were
hurting.

Now, they’re doing it all over again.

In early May, they pushed through rigged, racist maps designed to
eliminate TN-09’s identity as a majority-Black, Democratic district. TN
House Democrats stood together and made it clear that we would not stand
for this injustice.

So they retaliated.

Committee assignments aren’t ceremonial positions. They’re how state
lawmakers do the day-to-day work of representing our communities — from
hearing bills, shaping policy, and fighting for the needs of the People
who sent us there.

But no matter what, they can’t strip away our voice, our courage, and our
commitment to our People and neighborhoods. Civil rights icon and former
Representative John Lewis taught us to make good trouble — necessary
trouble.

With your support, we’ll keep doing just that,
Peter.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260521-jp.dTBcvO&refcode=em20260521-37802&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1005&akid=37802%2E1203867%2EdAsVL5 ]Please split $10 or more with our campaign and Justice Democrats in the
next 30 minutes so we have the resources to fight back against this latest
abuse of power.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260521-jp.dTBcvO&refcode=em20260521-37802&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1024&akid=37802%2E1203867%2EdAsVL5 ]Contribute $10

In Love and Service,

Justin J. Pearson

Good morning.

This note isn't going to all over our readers. Allow me to explain.

In 10 days, I'm launching _Flyover Updates_ , and I want you to be part of a special group.

I'm selecting an exclusive panel of _Flyover_ readers, including you, who I'm asking for a personal favor. [Sign up today](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskL2O6yAYRJ8Gd7H4tU1BcaXIXW67JcLwERMRsADHytuvvCtts-3W58xoNB83fTMhhnT_b56gms_agQvWNHA6wVEjtAZFP_ba3nk3yRkPR24rlKoppsMFiwslet5jvP4ESeeUB6DAOlBkHCWbGGayW5W34PEIgox4IsbjYeFCSmxBApHc-i6osxULSsiImeD94icuDBsmPjm3eIM4BhdaLv0jh9RW8PGdX1B6m59dVGtrW0XsH6IzovNvBdF5W3OCS92XaktY4DTZDE8TImJXRAUVBWzYAqTW7yVqSDY7cPpbOXlXlNuOEGOow4g4vp_ka0D7uwtfin4GAAD__5rYjFY) for _Flyover Updates_ and then give me your feedback. More about this below. **But first:** _Flyover Updates_ will be the most up-to-date news from the news source you already trust. It's an afternoon message with the biggest breaking stories of the day, delivered straight to your phone the moment they happen. You already start your morning more informed than most people. This is how you stay informed all day long. **Here are the three reasons you should sign up before we launch.** **1\. You won't miss important news.** A lot happens between 6 AM and when your head hits the pillow. Markets move. Storms develop. Major decisions come down from Washington or your statehouse. Right now, if it breaks during the day, you're probably waiting until tomorrow morning to find out _. Flyover Updates_ fixes that. An afternoon message with the most important stories that weren't in your morning edition. No waiting. No falling behind. Here's the best part. You won't be the one at the dinner table being caught up by your friends and family. You'll be the one catching them up. **2\. It's the news source you already read and trust.** You don't read _Flyover_ because you want more noise. You read because you want real news, told straight, without the spin. _Flyover Updates_ is the same thing. We're not just sending you whatever's trending on social media. This is _Flyover_ reporting, delivered the moment the story breaks. Same voice. Same standards. Just faster. **3\. It couldn't be easier, and there's zero risk.** No app to download. No new login. No commitment. You sign up, we send you one message in the afternoon, and you stay ahead of the news. That's it. If it's ever not for you, you can unsubscribe or pause anytime with a single reply. We're not in the business of cluttering your phone. If you don't love it, you're out in seconds. But we think you will love it. _**Sign up right[HERE](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskL2O6yAYRJ8Gd7H4tU1BcaXIXW67JcLwERMRsADHytuvvCtts-3W58xoNB83fTMhhnT_b56gms_agQvWNHA6wVEjtAZFP_ba3nk3yRkPR24rlKoppsMFiwslet5jvP4ESeeUB6DAOlBkHCWbGGayW5W34PEIgox4IsbjYeFCSmxBApHc-i6osxULSsiImeD94icuDBsmPjm3eIM4BhdaLv0jh9RW8PGdX1B6m59dVGtrW0XsH6IzovNvBdF5W3OCS92XaktY4DTZDE8TImJXRAUVBWzYAqTW7yVqSDY7cPpbOXlXlNuOEGOow4g4vp_ka0D7uwtfin4GAAD__5rYjFY). **_ And then here is the personal favor. Once you sign up and start receiving _Flyover Updates_ , tell me what you think. We launch in 10 days, and it's really important to me that you're one of our first readers and that I hear your feedback. Will you help me? Thanks for your time. Cole, CEO

| | | | | | Peter, running for Congress and flying 12,000lb Navy helicopters have some similarities. I know it sounds crazy, but just hear me out...

I’m Jen Kiggans: I’m a Navy veteran who flew H-46 and H-3 helicopters in the Persian Gulf. These massive machines are complicated; you’re sitting in a loud, tight, shaking cabin for hours on end, and you’re flying over waters where there’s no good place to land in case of emergency.
[In my service, I learned two important things:](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYwNTIxX1hPLUFILjExMDExN190MTkwNTk5NC0yMDY4JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MDUyMV9YTy1BSC4xMTAxMTdfdDE5MDU5OTQtMjA2OCJ9/oIy8dhNt0Acm9EuSg9RFfQ)

2\. We can only succeed by working as a team.
These lessons helped me when I felt the call to serve my country again in Congress. Even though I no longer wear a flight suit, I fight to put YOU and our country first every day in Congress.

name: Deb Haaland
subject: 🌶️ do you like green chile salsa? 🌶️
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/1102?refcode=jtk735-fr-ndem-header&t=1&akid=9728%2E400544%2ERw0Th1)
---
Hi friend, it's Deb Haaland. You know that I'm running for Governor of New Mexico to deliver progress for working families. **But did you also know that I love to cook?
**
One of my _favorite_ New Mexican staples to make is green chile salsa. The taste of fresh tomatoes and local green chile always brings me back home — to my family, our traditions, and the values that shaped me.

I love this recipe so much, in fact, it inspired me to start my very own salsa company to support my family. From finding capital to get started, to overseeing the work in the commercial kitchen, to delivering jars of salsa to mom and pop shops in Los Lunas, Belen, Bernalillo, and more — I was a part of every step, knowing I was supporting my child, contributing to our local economy, and bringing Pueblo culture into grocery stores across the state.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/8842?refcode=jtk735-fr-nd&t=2&akid=9728%2E400544%2ERw0Th1)
Food brings communities and people together, friend. When we share a home-cooked meal or baked goods, we share our traditions, our stories, and the care and time it takes to nourish our families. During this campaign, I've traveled across the state, meeting New Mexican families from all walks of life, breaking bread and sharing my vision for New Mexico.

I've shared my own struggles and listened to theirs. Together, we’ve made exciting plans for the future of New Mexico. I know New Mexicans want a governor who will fight for affordable healthcare, expand child care, make our communities safer, strengthen our schools, and protect our environment.
**That’s the kind of governor I will be.**
**I am ready on day one to get to work and deliver progress for our communities, including making it easier for local neighborhood markets to open and for grocery stores to carry home-grown food, especially to eliminate food deserts across New Mexico.**
[**_Pl_** _**ease, if you believe in my vision for a brighter New Mexico, chip in $5 or whatever you can spare now to help me become the next governor. NYT Headline 3/17/26: "The Scrappy Mayor Showing Democrats How It's Done"

I’ve spent my career rooting out corruption in NEPA. From the Scranton School Board to the Auditor General’s office to reforming City Hall as mayor, I have fought waste, cronyism, and abuse of trust so that government works for real people. Now, as your nominee, I’ll take this fight all the way to Washington.

Rob Bresnahan ran for this seat promising to ban congressional stock trading, and then became one of the most active traders in Congress. He’s using these trades to profit from his votes. His defense that a financial adviser handles everything does not answer the basic question of whose interests he is serving.

People in NEPA are tired of politicians who treat public office like a personal profit center. They want accountability. They want leaders who refuse special interest money and who close the loopholes that let public officials profit off their office. That is exactly what I will fight for in Congress. It’s time we have someone representing us who’s ready to get their hands dirty and do what it takes to bring back wins to NEPA. It’s time for someone scrappier in Congress.

Can you chip in $10 or whatever you can right now to strengthen our fight to fire Rob Bresnahan in November?

DONATE >> https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cognetti-slingshot-email-q2?amount=10&refcode=5.21.26_og_fr_nyt

Gratefully,

Mayor Paige Cognetti

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Elon Musk brought out his humanoid robot... name: Britney VanCitters
subject: The results are still coming in; here’s where we’re at
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/52126%20Election%20Results%20-%20email%20header.png]
Hi there,
The Primary Election was a couple of days ago, so results are still coming in, but here’s an overview of how our races currently look.
Many races are still too close to call while we patiently wait for every vote to be counted. From what we can see now, there are some mixed results for our OLCV-endorsed climate champions – not every race is leaning in our favor.
Here is the run-down of what we can currently share about our priority races:
* SD 3 – Ashland/Medford: TOO CLOSE TO CALL * As of writing this email, OLCV-endorsed candidate Tonia Moro trails Denise Krause by 209 votes.

* SD 15 - Hillsboro/Forest Grove: TOO CLOSE TO CALL * As of writing this, OLCV-endorsed challenger Myrna Muñoz leads incumbent Janeen Sollman by 155 votes!

* Washington County Chair: RUNOFF * With no candidate reaching over 50% of the vote, OLCV-endorsed Nafisa Fair appears to be headed to a runoff against Pam Treece.

* Deschutes County Commission Position 1: WIN * OLCV-endorsed climate scientist Jamie Collins has defeated the climate-denying incumbent! This is a huge win.

Every vote counts; we know this. And historically, younger and more progressive climate voters tend to vote closer to the deadline. So, with so many races too close to call yet, I am still hoping that the results will lean towards our climate candidates.
There is some good news I would like to highlight as we hold onto hope for the rest of these races:
* SD 11 – Keizer/Woodburn: WIN * OLCV-endorsed Virginia Stapleton has declared victory in this open contested senate seat. Now we look toward November to flip it from red to blue.

* SD 16 – North Coast: WIN * OLCV-endorsed Rachel Armitage won and heads to the general to win back this seat.

* SD 26 – Hood River/Sandy/Canby: WIN * OLCV-endorsed Nicole Bassett won and heads on to the general election where she intends to flip this seat.

I will be sending another follow up email once we know more.
With hope,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/Britney_signature-removebg-preview.png]
Britney VanCitters (she/her)
OLCV Political & Organizing Director

In the investment world, it has become almost passe to say that the stock market is the greatest builder of wealth in human history. Nevertheless, this adage continues to show its prophetic power year after year. In 2026, the S&P 500 index, which charts the 500 largest companies in America, is up over 8% year-to-date. This number far exceeds last year's percentage at this point, where the market was up a modest 1% or so. Even so, last year's total yearly returns were nearly 18% -- continuing a trend of strong returns throughout the 2020s.
As a result of the Trump presidency, which has slashed taxes, cut regulations, and committed trillions of dollars to domestic investment, the economy has entered an unprecedented golden age of growth and opportunity. More millionaires were minted since the President reclaimed the mantle of power than at any other point in history - and 2026 is looking to lead the charts for newly minted billionaires worldwide, with an average pace of over one new billionaire being created each day (the vast majority of these, of course, being concentrated in the United States).

For these reasons, coupled with the sentiment that a settlement may soon be reached in both the Middle East, with the Iran war in the process of winding down (or at the very least, having reached a workable detente), and now, rekindled talks of a peace deal in Eastern Europe, the global economy is well-positioned to go on a dominant run as it enters the summer months.
This sentiment is backed by cold hard data: the recent job report released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics shows the United States adding roughly 120,000 new jobs in April, driven by healthcare and services, surpassing the expectations of most economists. Meanwhile, investor sentiment remains doggedly bullish - with nearly 40% prognosticating a continued upswing in equities markets based on the latest AAI Investor Sentiment Survey. Though consumer sentiment remains slightly dampened, mostly driven by higher gas and oil prices, that looks to soon change too with peace once more on the table in the Middle East.
This week Marco Rubio, the Secretary of State, is breaking bread with Pope Leo, the first American pope, and one of the staunchest critics of the Iran war among the global community: a telltale that tensions are simmering down. Hence, if all bodes well, oil prices will likely decline in the months ahead - particularly as the Strait of Hormuz gradually reopens. Even with these bumps in the road, consumer spending continues to increase quarter over quarter. Spending may be increasing at a slightly decreasing rate, but the underlying sentiment trends positively - a sign of American economic power, and generally strong economic momentum that permeates sectors corporate and retail alike.

* * *
* * *
The economy is strong, with signs of even strengthening dominance in the months and years ahead. Innovative technology, driven by AI and robotics, continues to fuel the economic engine. This has offset many of the problems caused by the Middle East war, and has had ripple effects on investors, both large and small, given how much weight a handful of particularly productive tech companies pull. Investors who put their money in broad-based index funds linked to the tech-heavy Dow Jones Industrial Average or the S&P 500 experience the upside effects secondhand, even if they are not directly invested in AI startups.
The accelerated growth reflected in these indices are primarily, if not exclusively, driven by emerging technologies: which increasingly self-conceptualize as an intrinsic element of the overall economy and not simply the bespoke niche technology may have been fifteen or twenty years ago. This is captured by AI's effects on everything from semiconductors to renewable energy to medical technology; it continues to have a revolutionary impact on job markets globally and is poised to kickstart a more revolutionary transformation on mankind within the next five to ten years.

This number far exceeds last year's percentage at this point, where the market was up a modest 1% or so. Even so, last year's total yearly returns were nearly 18% -- continuing a trend of strong returns throughout the 2020s. As a result of the Trump presidency, which has slashed taxes, cut regulations, and committed trillions of dollars to domestic investment, the economy has entered an unprecedented golden age of growth and opportunity. More millionaires were minted since the President reclaimed the mantle of power than at any other point in history - and 2026 is looking to lead the charts for newly minted billionaires worldwide, with an average pace of over one new billionaire being created each day (the vast majority of these, of course, being concentrated in the United States). This sentiment is backed by cold hard data: the recent job report released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics shows the United States adding roughly 120,000 new jobs in April, driven by healthcare and services, surpassing the expectations of most economists. Meanwhile, investor sentiment remains doggedly bullish - with nearly 40% prognosticating a continued upswing in equities markets based on the latest AAI Investor Sentiment Survey. Though consumer sentiment remains slightly dampened, mostly driven by higher gas and oil prices, that looks to soon change too with peace once more on the table in the Middle East. This week Marco Rubio, the Secretary of State, is breaking bread with Pope Leo, the first American pope, and one of the staunchest critics of the Iran war among the global community: a telltale that tensions are simmering down. Hence, if all bodes well, oil prices will likely decline in the months ahead - particularly as the Strait of Hormuz gradually reopens. Even with these bumps in the road, consumer spending continues to increase quarter over quarter. The accelerated growth reflected in these indices are primarily, if not exclusively, driven by emerging technologies: which increasingly self-conceptualize as an intrinsic element of the overall economy and not simply the bespoke niche technology may have been fifteen or twenty years ago. name: Voto Latino
subject: Republicans are counting on Latino voters to not show up in November
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
Latino voters are going to be the margin of victory this November.
#
Peter,
A recent _Axios_ article points out something we’ve known for a very long time.
**Latino voters are going to be the margin of victory in November.**
[****](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260521-1-ak.rfqVQ2&amount=3&refcode=em20260521-160&t=1&akid=160%2E1366028%2EuCfh03)
[**Will you rush in $3 donation today to help Voto Latino register and turn out Latino voters in the districts that will decide control of Congress?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260521-1-ak.rfqVQ2&amount=3&refcode=em20260521-160&t=2&akid=160%2E1366028%2EuCfh03)
After 2024, a lot of pundits rushed to declare that Latino voters were “shifting right for good.”

Peter,

On this day in 1919, the House of Representatives passed what would become the 19th Amendment.

It was a turning point after years of organizing, marching, and fighting for something that should have never been out of reach in the first place—**the right for women to have a voice in our democracy.**

But even that moment wasn't the finish line. For many women, especially Black, brown, and Indigenous women, that right remained out of reach for decades. It took _the Voting Rights Act of 1965_ to begin to make the promise of the 19th Amendment real for **everyone.**

The right to vote has never been something we could take for granted. And today, the fight to protect women's right to vote is still ongoing. People in powerful positions, right-wing influencers with large followings, and the president of the United States himself, are pushing ideas that would drag us backward, including questioning whether women should have the right to vote at all.

Last year, United States Secretary of Defense, Pete Hegseth, openly shared an interview with a pastor who argued that women shouldn't have a role in public decision-making and should instead defer to men in their households. **Others have gone even further, calling the 19th Amendment a mistake and floating ideas that would take voting power away from women entirely.**

As a doctor, I've spent my career listening to people and advocating for them. As a mom, I think about the kind of country we're shaping for the next generation. And as your representative, I believe protecting the right to vote is one of the most basic responsibilities we have. We can honor the progress we've made while also being clear about what's at stake right now. Friend,

The FIFA World Cup kicks off in New Jersey in just 36 days, and FIFA game ticketing has stolen too many ideas from anti-consumer Ticketmaster.

Tickets that were supposed to make the World Cup accessible to everyday New Jerseyans have nearly doubled in price. Fans who paid top dollar for the best seats got shuffled to worse ones, and then FIFA turned around and sold the good seats again at twice the price. And the resale market? FIFA takes a 30% cut from buyers and sellers combined.

This isn't what a World Cup on American soil is supposed to look like. It's supposed to be a boost for local businesses, a celebration for soccer fans, and a moment of pride for our communities. Instead, we have what feels like a mere cash grab.

Nellie wants accountability and isn't letting that stand.

Earlier this month, she and her colleague Frank Pallone, who is top Dem on the committee overseeing consumer protection, demanded answers directly from FIFA President Gianni Infantino. They called out the hidden pricing, the misleading seat maps, and the artificial ticket scarcity that's leaving fans frustrated and shut out.

That's Nellie. When someone — no matter how big or powerful — is taking advantage of New Jerseyans, she fights back. Chip in today to keep her in that fight. [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/pou_em?refcode=260521_tp_fifa2_l1&amount=10]

| Denver doesn't need another politician who tells working people to be patient while the rent goes up, health care gets more expensive, wages fall behind, and billionaires keep getting their calls returned first.
We need politicians with a backbone.
Who believe health care is a right, housing should not be treated like a casino for private equity, workers deserve unions, immigrants deserve dignity, and our tax dollars should not fund genocide.
And we need public servants who are honest about why so much of Washington is broken - that too many people in power are funded by the same corporations and special interests they are supposed to regulate.
That is the heart of this campaign.
We are running against a 30-year incumbent because Denver deserves a representative who understands what it means to live in this economy right now. Not 30 years ago. Not in theory. Right now.
So I'm asking:

I fully support a ban on Members of Congress and anyone in the administration from owning or trading stocks. I completely divested from stocks when I was elected to avoid conflicts of interest.

Trump can't say the same. In a recent financial disclosure, it was revealed that he made 3,700 stock trades in the first quarter of the year.

It's a shocking statistic that comes out to over 40 trades per day. While working families struggle to make ends meet, Trump is getting richer and richer.

Many of these trades involved companies directly affected by his decisions – Nvidia, Paramount, Netflix, Oracle, Microsoft, Boeing, eBay, and hundreds more.

Did his stock trades influence his decisions? Or did his decisions influence his stock trades?

Either way, the scale of corruption out of the Trump Administration is out of control – and unlike anything this country has seen before.

I refuse to let this become our new normal. If you agree, will you sign my petition demanding a ban on Trump and Congress from trading stocks?

Don't miss our deep-dive video today on the MAJOR Polis Tina Peters' drama, and the other commutation that the Dems seem to be silent on. Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** Polis told a University of Denver audience he has [no regrets](https://link.email.joinrmv.) over commuting Tina Peters' sentence. Colorado voters will decide in November on Senate Bill 135, which critics say would [dismantle TABOR refunds](https://link.email.joinrmv.) under the guise of education funding. Business leaders told Polis at a Chamber luncheon [Colorado is showing "cracks" in competitiveness](https://link.email.joinrmv.). And Denver, Jefferson County, and Aurora have each [imposed data center moratoriums](https://link.email.joinrmv.) as Denver Water drains Antero Reservoir for the first time since 2002.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** Trump-endorsed Ed Gallrein [defeated Rep. Thomas Massie](https://link.email.joinrmv.) in Kentucky's 4th District primary. [VP Vance named Tina Peters](https://link.email.joinrmv.) as a candidate for the Trump administration's new $1.8 billion "Anti-Weaponization Fund." And a California voting activist pleaded guilty to a two-decade scheme [paying homeless people to sign election petitions](https://link.email.joinrmv.) — which FBI Director Kash Patel says signals a broader federal crackdown on election fraud.
**✍️ Commentary Spotlight...** Male athlete AB Hernandez [swept three girls' track events](https://link.email.joinrmv.) at California's Southern Sectionals, displacing competitors including Reese Hogan, who said "it's disappointing to go into a competition knowing you already lost." Two commentators argue [coastal desalination](https://link.email.joinrmv.) — pointing to San Diego's Carlsbad plant — could [ease Colorado River shortages](https://link.email.joinrmv.) and protect Colorado's water rights. And the Colorado Accountability Project [flags the PUC sunset bill](https://link.email.joinrmv.) for quietly removing the only cost guardrail on renewable energy pricing.
This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, May 21, 2026.

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado killed its only data center water bills. Cities are filling the gap themselves.](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
Colorado spent a year trying to answer a basic question: should companies building massive AI data centers be required to disclose how much water they use? The answer, as of May 11, was no.
Senate Bill 26-102 would have required operators of new large data centers to report annual water use to state health officials. A companion measure, House Bill 26-1030, sought to attract data centers through voluntary tax incentives tied to water efficiency standards. HB26-1030 died in committee on May 7. SB26-102 followed four days later.
238 lobbyists registered positions on one or both bills on behalf of 221 clients, according to Secretary of State records. Five days after the legislature adjourned, Denver City Council unanimously passed a one-year moratorium on new data center construction, naming water consumption as one of the things the city will now regulate — joining Aurora, which has enforced its own data center water restrictions since 2023. The next day, Jefferson County voted on a similar temporary ban.
