**[Coastal desalination could save Colorado’s water. The pushback? Cost](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY MICHAEL J BADAGLIACCO "MJB", [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Colorado's water rights are under pressure:** The 1922 Colorado River Compact allocated 3.86 million acre-feet annually to Colorado, but actual river flows since 2000 average only 12.4 million acre-feet — far below projections — leaving Lake Mead and Lake Powell under declared shortage conditions while Lower Basin states consume their full legal shares.
* **The technology to fix it already exists:** Montrose Mayor Michael Badagliacco points to San Diego's Carlsbad Desalination Plant — producing 50 million gallons per day — as proof the technology works, and argues small modular nuclear reactors could power expanded coastal facilities that would restore reservoir storage without touching Colorado's water rights.
* **Cost is the only objection — and it's a weak one:** Congressman Jeff Hurd cited expense as the barrier, but Badagliacco counters that water use across the basin generates more than $20 billion in annual economic benefits, and that crop losses, food price increases, and long-term economic contraction make inaction far more costly.

**[What’s Likely to Change at Colorado’s Public Utilities Commission](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** [COLORADO ACCOUNTABILITY PROJECT](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **A win for transparency, but just barely:** After bipartisan outcry, sponsors stripped a provision from HB26-1326 that would have allowed PUC commissioners to deliberate privately — which even the state's own regulatory reform office called a "dramatic departure from traditional notions of open meetings" — and moved the next sunset review from 2037 to 2033.
* **The quiet rewiring no one is talking about:** The bill removes the only cost guardrail requiring examination of whether renewables are truly cheaper, expands who can appeal local land-use decisions to the PUC, and redirects utility penalties toward social-policy programs — a drift from the PUC's core mission of setting just and reasonable rates.
* **An unresolved contradiction at the heart of Colorado's energy policy:** The PUC is simultaneously mandated to meet greenhouse gas targets and deliver reliable power at the lowest cost — two directives critics say are fundamentally incompatible, and which HB26-1326 does nothing to resolve.

This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, May 21, 2026. – Team RMV | TODAY'S TOP STORIES BY SHAINA COLE, Colorado spent a year trying to answer a basic question: should companies building massive AI data centers be required to disclose how much water they use? The answer, as of May 11, was no. Senate Bill 26-102 would have required operators of new large data centers to report annual water use to state health officials. A companion measure, House Bill 26-1030, sought to attract data centers through voluntary tax incentives tied to water efficiency standards. HB26-1030 died in committee on May 7. SB26-102 followed four days later. 238 lobbyists registered positions on one or both bills on behalf of 221 clients, according to Secretary of State records. Five days after the legislature adjourned, Denver City Council unanimously passed a one-year moratorium on new data center construction, naming water consumption as one of the things the city will now regulate — joining Aurora, which has enforced its own data center water restrictions since 2023. The next day, Jefferson County voted on a similar temporary ban. | Be part of history at Freedom Festival 2026. Celebrate America’s 250th and Colorado’s 150th with with 2000+ patriots: two unforgettable days of speakers, action, community, and FUN for the whole family at the Douglas County Fairgrounds. America only turns 250 once. Colorado only turns 150 once. Secure your tickets now and be part of it. | BY MICHAEL J BADAGLIACCO "MJB", Colorado's water rights are under pressure: The 1922 Colorado River Compact allocated 3.86 million acre-feet annually to Colorado, but actual river flows since 2000 average only 12.4 million acre-feet — far below projections — leaving Lake Mead and Lake Powell under declared shortage conditions while Lower Basin states consume their full legal shares. The technology to fix it already exists: Montrose Mayor Michael Badagliacco points to San Diego's Carlsbad Desalination Plant — producing 50 million gallons per day — as proof the technology works, and argues small modular nuclear reactors could power expanded coastal facilities that would restore reservoir storage without touching Colorado's water rights. Cost is the only objection — and it's a weak one: Congressman Jeff Hurd cited expense as the barrier, but Badagliacco counters that water use across the basin generates more than $20 billion in annual economic benefits, and that crop losses, food price increases, and long-term economic contraction make inaction far more costly. | The Rocky Mountain Voice is a 501(c)(3) that exists to promote informed civic engagement and the principles of self-governance through enterprise reporting on public policy, politics, government, and culture throughout the state of Colorado. The quiet rewiring no one is talking about: The bill removes the only cost guardrail requiring examination of whether renewables are truly cheaper, expands who can appeal local land-use decisions to the PUC, and redirects utility penalties toward social-policy programs — a drift from the PUC's core mission of setting just and reasonable rates. An unresolved contradiction at the heart of Colorado's energy policy: The PUC is simultaneously mandated to meet greenhouse gas targets and deliver reliable power at the lowest cost — two directives critics say are fundamentally incompatible, and which HB26-1326 does nothing to resolve. | ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | MAY 19 Democrats organized a censure push over Tina Peters. It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 _ _ and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. **But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250****th**** birthday.**

Patriot, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. **Patriot, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you.** **[In light of America’s 250th birthday and the special opportunity we have to honor veterans this year, will you chip in today to help support the parade with a gift of $25, $50, $75, $150, or more?](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=0857c9d865b9444696f2540bc49bf7dc&_e=GuRaP3-KXFVxs5oHxsrBXbqjA65dL-F5loAqgrlY_eWqNGeIWfa-rnLj1kktLNDfuqIUz-uCCxvwo0F9bJ2MjwDu5VvChw3p-3pvLHTgMsxjaQj8omsL-XUJ4DRnPsxH9gTKkEzURGh3AtdxVd-MeUnmL7aPzC7rqoHa3I6V5ySzwgd4tVIJysQGkmsOfdghDogpoRCuHToMlG_f8y9tAJh6odCDhOZlaeX0ZpYr9TPwovpC_9k1Aw4xX6mjROB4uCq1PbJvRwps1LojuWcAdubADUr-yS336nWwFlAXzNTLxe7QxFS7GxFda1_cYiApntzZQKjSi5K9zWe06cZnPGjiYPOxLdn2iGRq3oNyoiRsOnD9sjnOzWS7bx9t8yazoCROeqyeU3WrCT2jR4uY5-LBFEMNhGX7MuPTAyAn9v_oXZTV2boiilPQPaqTtoTSbCsXcmT29FHlvE3vmiQLiaL8l1McQbojTyDlqiVkugnCJC8__6nI7ycdFFnSnaFAs3rL2wXDFvOEz_Q-1Ev4XZOaWn7D8myV8n2RYkFeaY24xEM3EvM8sL6pG65cDdVO1sFUW1od0hJQwWk9dY45zzd3qHgSdp29gOkbASzwR3agOBCC31IO_aaFcczK-5wu0fWaxK86UyoOeQ554reOyzNZ_rj80UOZEe0cNFYf958j-XLkJuxdUFimboSbhNGv48I4hUXdpfP4O9KFiunKvg%3D%3D)**

In fact, _the entire parade_ costs about as much as just THREE balloons in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade or TWO floats in the Rose Bowl Parade! _That means that every dollar that's contributed by a generous American like you makes a difference for this important event._ **But I want to reiterate that American Veterans Center does not take ANY federal funding for this event. | | Your support of the American Veterans Center not only helps the parade, but also supports great programs like:
---
* Record hundreds of oral histories of veterans from World War II to today before we lose these stories forever.

* Hold our annual American Veterans Conference, which allows young cadets a chance to hear first-hand from veterans from WWII, Korea, Vietnam, and our modern wars.

* Produce veteran-focused T.V. documentaries and specials that remind Americans the price of our freedom.

clean_body: | | | Patriot, It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Patriot, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Patriot, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. The 2026 National Memorial Day Parade is a once-in-a-lifetime moment where we need to do all we can to honor our country and our veterans. Bigger crowds. More veterans. More young people learning what courage, service, and sacrifice really mean. Historically, AVC has been able to do this at a fraction of what other major public events cost to put on each year. In fact, the entire parade costs about as much as just THREE balloons in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade or TWO floats in the Rose Bowl Parade! That means that every dollar that's contributed by a generous American like you makes a difference for this important event. But I want to reiterate that American Veterans Center does not take ANY federal funding for this event. It is funded entirely by private citizens like you who want to honor those who have sacrificed so much for our country. | | Your support of the American Veterans Center not only helps the parade, but also supports great programs like: Record hundreds of oral histories of veterans from World War II to today before we lose these stories forever. Hold our annual American Veterans Conference, which allows young cadets a chance to hear first-hand from veterans from WWII, Korea, Vietnam, and our modern wars. Produce veteran-focused T.V. documentaries and specials that remind Americans the price of our freedom. But of course, the National Memorial Day Parade is AVC's flagship event honoring America's veterans. And this year's parade will be the largest in their history of hosting the parade. If you've been looking for an opportunity to give back to those who have given so much for our freedom, this is one of the best possible ways you could do it. And for a special group of veterans, this might be one of the last chances we get. You see, with each year that goes by, we lose more and more of our World War II veterans, and for the few we have remaining, traveling to Washington, D.C., for the parade is difficult. | | | | | WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. But this may be the last year we have the opportunity to have these brave men and women with us for the parade. This year is a rare moment when living witnesses to World War II and America 's 250**th birthday overlap. And no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you. On Memorial Day - not just this momentous year of military milestones, but every year - please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. Visit a local veterans' cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. I believe that while we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, we can always do a little more. Patriot, thank you for your support of America 's heroes. Sincerely, Gary Sinise Honarary Grand MarshalNational Memorial Day Parade P.S. Patriot, America is stepping into its 250th year, and this Memorial Day begins that national remembrance. Veterans across generations have given their lives to defend America and all she stands for. And for the Greatest Generation in particular, this may be the last time they're able to join us at this year's National Memorial Day Parade. There's no better send-off we can give them than to make sure they're present to honor their fallen brethren during America's 250th birthday. Derek, Republicans are going after your right to vote. And honestly, they're not even trying to be subtle about it.
**[I'll get into it – but first, if you believe every American should have the freedom to vote and have that vote actually count, will you take my Democracy Survey now?](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/53404?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&t=1&akid=10772%2E434096%2EgLQc-N)**

The Supreme Court just gutted the Voting Rights Act – a law that has protected communities of color from being gerrymandered for nearly 60 years. **And Republican-led states are ALREADY rushing to redraw their maps because of it. They're also ...**
👉 Pushing the SAVE America Act to gut mail-in voting and make it way harder to register to vote.
👉 Continuing to spread conspiracy theories about widespread voter fraud, which have been debunked time and again.
👉 Courting super PACs and dark-money groups to buy our elections.
This isn't normal.
**And with midterm elections just months away, they're only going to push harder.**
Look – I'm not going anywhere. I'm going to keep fighting like hell in the Senate to protect our democracy. That's not even a question.

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: We should be funding health care, not cruelty.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
I’ve introduced the Medicare For All Act in every session of Congress because every single person in this country deserves to get the care they need.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260521-6265-footer&t=1&akid=6265%2E420207%2E7ep-Tz)
Peter,
Right now, your tax dollars are paying for masked ICE agents to break down doors in the middle of the night — to kidnap and detain people without warrants, tear families apart, and send our neighbors to countries they’ve never known, without due process.
The truth is ICE isn’t making our communities safer. They’re just making us more afraid.
And while billions of dollars go toward that cruelty, Americans are skipping medications, drowning in medical debt, or going without care altogether. The situation is so bad that health care is now the number one cost concern for working people in this country.
**We should be funding health care, not cruelty.**
I’ve introduced the Medicare For All Act in every session of Congress because every single person in this country deserves to get the care they need from birth to death, without the fine print or a for-profit insurance company deciding where you go or what treatments you can have access to.
And an overwhelming number of voters agree. **90% of Democrats, 60% of independents, and even 1 in 5 Republicans support Medicare For All.** Voters aren’t looking for incremental changes anymore. _They want us to go big._
I’m not going to stop until we get it done, but I’m counting on the support of this grassroots movement every step of the way. I don’t take a dime from corporate PACs or lobbyists — it’s supporters like you, pitching in $3 at a time, who power this movement.
[**Peter, if you’re with me, can I count on you to pitch in $3 today to help us fight for health care over ICE?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260521.kPCjz4&refcode=em20260521-6265&amount=3&t=2&akid=6265%2E420207%2E7ep-Tz)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260521.kPCjz4&amount=3&refcode=em20260521-6265&t=21&akid=6265%2E420207%2E7ep-Tz)**
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20260521-2287-foote&t=1001&akid=2287%2E342411%2E_NZDEx ]Squad Victory Fund

Peter,

Trump’s ICE crackdowns terrorized immigrant communities across Minnesota.
Families were separated. Communities were targeted. Kids went to bed
afraid that a parent could be ripped from them overnight.

Now, a former ICE prosecutor wants a seat in Congress — and she’s running
against Ilhan.

Someone who once helped defend deportations and uphold ICE in court is
trying to replace one of the boldest voices in Congress fighting against
that very system.

We refuse to accept this version of “justice.”

This race is about whether the people who enabled ICE get rewarded with
political power, or whether we have a progressive leader who is unafraid
to speak truth to power.

Ilhan has never backed down.

Not when Trump targeted immigrant communities. Not when the right wing
spent years attacking her for speaking out. And not when powerful people
told her to stay quiet. She fights for immigrants, working people, and
communities too often treated as disposable by those in power.

That’s exactly why they’re coming for her seat. They want to silence one
of the strongest voices standing up to ICE abuses and defending immigrant
communities.

So we’re fighting back the same way we always do: with people power.

Squad Victory Fund is organizing in communities, talking directly to
voters, and building the grassroots movement needed to defend Ilhan from
this coordinated effort to push Minnesota backward.

| | I believe health care is a right. **That means**** _every_****person in Northwest Washington and across the country should be able to see a doctor, fill a prescription, and get the care they need without worrying about whether they can afford it.** That belief has guided my work in Congress. **I reintroduced the Influenza Act, legislation to strengthen our nation's ability to prevent and respond to seasonal and pandemic flu.** Every year, influenza sends children and adults to the hospital, forces working families to miss school and paychecks, and claims lives that could be saved. My bill would invest in faster vaccine development, expand access to flu shots, strengthen public health infrastructure, and combat misinformation so families can make informed decisions about their health. I also joined more than 250 Democratic members of Congress in urging the Supreme Court to protect access to mifepristone, a safe and effective medication that has been used by millions of patients for more than 25 years. **Restricting access to medication abortion would put medically appropriate care further out of reach, especially for people in rural communities and for those who already face barriers to accessing health care.** These efforts are part of a larger commitment to ensuring everyone in Northwest Washington can get the care they need. I support universal, affordable health coverage because no one should have to choose between paying the bills and getting the care they need. I support protecting reproductive freedom because politicians should not interfere in personal medical decisions. And I support strengthening public health systems because preventing illness saves lives and lowers costs for families. **Health care should be high-quality, affordable, and accessible to everyone.** That is what I am working toward in Congress. Peter,

**I just said something in Washington that apparently rattled a few cages.**

Good.

**If the government shuts down, Senators shouldn’t get paid.**

And I’ll tell you something else while we’re here—I’ve seen this movie before.

Democrats may very well try to force a shutdown before the midterms because chaos is so good for their politics. They create the mess, Republicans get blamed, and the media acts like it’s the gospel truth.

That’s the game.

_**Now, where I come from, if you don’t work, you don’t get paid. Simple as that.**_

**But in Washington, some folks think they ought to keep collecting paychecks while the country deals with the headache they caused.**

Well, that dog won’t hunt.

No pay. No leaving town. Stay here and fix it.

Because if Republicans let Democrats turn this place into a circus right before the election, we could lose this majority faster than a snowball melts in July.

I don’t intend to let that happen.

He wants to mark the anniversary of our independence by handing out 250 more get-out-of-jail-free cards – almost certainly for people who have attacked the very principles included in the Declaration of Independence. Over the last two years, we’ve watched Trump pardon thousands of January 6 rioters, grant clemency to family members of prominent Republican donors, and even pardon foreign heads of state who had been convicted of massive drug trafficking offenses. He’s already handed out more than 1,600 pardons this term alone. Trump treats presidential power like a rewards program for anyone who helps him subvert the law or lines his pockets, and that kind of impunity destroys our democracy. I used Congress’s oversight power to hold Trump accountable as lead counsel in the Ukraine impeachment, and I will use it again to do the same when we take back the House in November. Holding this administration accountable requires leaders in Congress who know how to fight back — and who have actually done it. Nobody knows how to do that better than me, and I will do it again when we take back the House in November. **Peter, I can’t re-elect myself to Congress. Supporters like you sent me to fight for our democracy and working families and I’ll continue to do just that, with enough grassroots support.** [**My primary is fast approaching and June 23 will be here before we know it. | **__A Letter from the Desk of Rep. Elise Stefanik__**
---
Peter,
---
President Trump has made it clear that he’ll do whatever it takes to WIN the midterms because he knows how vital our House Majority is to passing the America First agenda: _**“We must keep the Majority _at_ _all_ _costs_.”**_
---
No one understands that better than me.
---
Last year, I did what our country needed and withdrew my nomination to serve in President Trump’s cabinet to remain in the House and _protect_ our razor-thin Majority.
---
_And thank God I did. My vote was ultimately the tie-breaking vote to pass the President’s Big Beautiful Bill and grant tax cuts to millions of American families!_
---
For me, America First was never just a campaign slogan.
---
For every remaining minute that I have the honor to serve you in Congress, doing what’s right for our country will _**always**_ be my top priority.
---

clean_body: No one understands that better than me. | A Letter from the Desk of Rep. Elise Stefanik Peter, President Trump has made it clear that he’ll do whatever it takes to WIN the midterms because he knows how vital our House Majority is to passing the America First agenda: “We must keep the Majority at all costs.” No one understands that better than me. Last year, I did what our country needed and withdrew my nomination to serve in President Trump’s cabinet to remain in the House and protect our razor-thin Majority. And thank God I did. My vote was ultimately the tie-breaking vote to pass the President’s Big Beautiful Bill and grant tax cuts to millions of American families! For me, America First was never just a campaign slogan. For every remaining minute that I have the honor to serve you in Congress, doing what’s right for our country will always be my top priority. That’s why, even though I’m no longer running for reelection, I’m still committed to doing everything I can to help the President DEFEND his Majority. Since I no longer need funds for my own campaign, I’ve decided the most effective way I can help is to use my grassroots donor network –among the most powerful in the entire country – to help America First Republicans WIN the key battleground races of the midterms. After all the sacrifices I’ve made for our House Majority, you can rest assured that I’m going to spend every second I have left in Congress fighting to stop the Democrats from seizing control and DESTROYING everything we’ve fought so hard to accomplish. But as we approach yet another critical fundraising deadline, I have no choice but to ask dedicated America First patriots like YOU to join me. Thank you and God Bless, Rep. Elise Stefanik Paid for by Team Elise, a joint fundraising committee authorized by and composed of E-PAC and Save New York. www.teamelise.org PO Box 100 Guilderland Center NY 12085 |

Not Democrats who wait to see what leadership thinks, who take the safe vote, who disappear when conversations get uncomfortable. That frustration has been building for years, and it is finally showing up in races across the country. Seth has never been afraid to stand up for what is right: pushing for age limits in Congress and term limits for committee chairs, questioning the war in Iran, banning his team from polymarket betting, and calling for the prosecution of ICE agents. They ultimately were the right call. That's what this moment is calling for: not just a party that is in opposition to Trump, but one with the spine to match the urgency of what we're up against. Seth is making that case everywhere he goes, and people are responding to it. subject: This is what California politics looks like when money calls the shots.

body:
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=41395%2E3422442%2EjXdmIi)
Peter, here’s what we’re up against:
1. Two MAGA Republicans who want to drag California backward.
2. Tom Steyer—a billionaire who’s trying to buy this seat with $197 million of his own money.
3. Xavier Becerra, who took maximum contributions from Big Oil, sold out to corporations, and is now abandoning single-payer health care.

**This is what California politics looks like when money calls the shots.**
Katie Porter is different.
She's a single mom of three who’s lived the impossible math that too many families are living right now—the rising costs, the child care bill that eats a paycheck, the health insurance that doesn't cover what you need.
That's why she's running: to lower housing costs, to make child care free, to win single-payer health care, and to eliminate California income tax entirely for anyone making under $100,000.
Katie doesn't take billionaire checks or sell out to corporations. What she has is more than 100,000 people who've chipped in what they can, when they can.
_The only way to beat that kind of money is to drown it out with people._
We're in the final sprint. Every voter Katie reaches, every town hall hosted, every dollar raised in the next two weeks determines whether she's on November's ballot.
**[We’re almost at the finish line, Peter. Can you chip in $5 today to make sure Katie breaks into the top two and secures a spot on the November ballot?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260521_2_ak.cvRVKj&refcode=em20260521-41395&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=41395%2E3422442%2EjXdmIi)**

The lawsuit the Supreme Court agreed to hear isn't about fairness. It's not about so-called "election integrity," because millions of taxpayers' dollars have been wasted on state investigations looking for mail-in ballot fraud that simply does not exist.
This lawsuit is a political ploy to suppress legitimate mail-in ballots that are postmarked by Election Day and potentially delayed by the U.S. Postal Service. This lawsuit targets our fellow citizens who have done nothing wrong and might have their vote suppressed through delays out of their control. And it's all because the political party that brought the lawsuit knows that those delayed ballots are more likely to have been cast by voters for the other party and not themselves.
We cannot let anyone get away with such a cynical attempt at hidden voter suppression, no matter who controls the Supreme Court. RUSH $35 or more right now to help us spread the word about this lawsuit and defend the right to vote across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=052126_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
DemocracyDocket: SCOTUS to Hear GOP Lawsuit That Could Radically Restrict Mail Voting [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=052126_2&amount=25]
Team: Mail-in ballots are under attack again.
The Supreme Court agreed to hear arguments in RNC v. Wetzel, a lawsuit challenging Mississippi’s law allowing a five-day grace period for late-arriving ballots mailed by Election Day. In simpler terms, it's a case about whether your vote will count if you mail it on or before Election Day, but your ballot arrives after Election Day.
It's clear why a political party -- in this case, the Republican National Committee (RNC) -- is claiming that states must reject ballots that arrive after Election Day. Doing so would potentially disenfranchise a large number of voters, restricting the number of participants in an election. And the data is clear, over the last several election cycles, Republicans have been outnumbered in the use of mail-in ballots.
The RNC is making a blunt decision that their ability to win elections matters more than your vote. It's a cynical attempt to stay in power by suppressing ballots that are delivered late by the postal service. It's the kind of partisan work that shows they'd rather believe in their own power and control than the principles of democracy, of a country where all our votes should count, regardless of party.

Our position is clear: If your ballot was postmarked by Election Day, it should count.
This shouldn't be a partisan question. No political party -- Democrat, Republican, Green, Working Families, Libertarian, Reform, Conservative -- should be against voting. No party in our democracy should want to restrict the fundamental right of our fellow citizens to make their voice heard through voting.
But now we're facing a case where the Supreme Court’s decision could strike down or uphold laws in 16 states (and Washington D.C.) allowing late-arriving ballots postmarked on or before Election Day to be counted if they arrive within a set grace period.
How do we know what is at stake? Data from the 2024 Massachusetts elections shows that their three-day grace period for ballots to arrive after Election Day resulted in a 60% drop in rejected ballots as compared to no grace period. That means thousands of votes still counted, more than 1.5% of the total vote count. In a close election, that 1.5% could easily mean the difference between winning and losing.
Our fundamental right to vote should matter so much more than a partisan desperation to win. Chip in $35 or whatever you can to help us defend the use of mail-in ballots and make every vote count in elections nationwide >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=052126_2&amount=35]

For days last week, black and yellow smoke poured out of the Suncor refinery into Commerce City again.
The second time in a month.
For years, Suncor has poisoned our air while Colorado families pay the price with asthma, headaches, cancer risks, and toxic air in their neighborhoods. And what happens when they get caught?
Let’s look at the facts: Suncor made more than $2 billion in profit in a single quarter. And last year, Governor Polis fined them $2 million for polluting our air.
We did the math. For Suncor, that’s the equivalent of a $20 parking ticket for a Colorado family.
Suncor didn’t feel that fine. It wasn’t a punishment. They drove through a community, threw $20 out the window, and kept poisoning our air.
That’s what I mean when I say the wealthy and powerful play by a completely different set of rules. And here’s the truth: this pollution is not an accident. It’s a business decision.
I’m the only candidate in this attorney general race with a real, specific plan to hold corporate polluters accountable.
People ask me, well how much should companies like Suncor pay? Enough that they stop harming Colorado families.
And if they can’t stop polluting, then we should shut them the hell down.
That’s what the law is supposed to do: protect people, not corporate profits. But I need your help to build the kind of campaign strong enough to take on billion-dollar corporations and the politicians who protect them.
Will you contribute to my grassroots campaign today so we can fight back against corporate polluters, hold Suncor accountable, and build an attorney general’s office that works for people, not powerful corporations? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_dhs_email-26q2?refcode=X_260521_suncor_act]

They spent big to defeat Tammy in 2024 (didn’t work 💅). Now, they’ve already committed $300 million to holding the Senate majority this year, with more on the way. We don’t have a crystal ball, but we know this much: Republican super PACs are going to spend whatever it takes to protect their majority, drown out Democrats, and stop our momentum before Election Day. Rallies alone don’t win elections. Grassroots organizing does. | | |
---
| Hi folks, This is Emily, Saikat’s campaign manager.

The primary is on June 2nd, less than two weeks away, so I thought it’d be a good time for us to pull back the curtain on where things stand.

You can help us sprint through the finish line by **[chipping in what you’re able today](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqu9GgNqQBZQbHGys41Ff66GdRsXl3aU86FUQm8hkp73cI0TbF-sjuAc3AWQCrU7eDcudKyg63pvIzATs21OBv0wNtc3j1nPZaFEXIzIN7_K_fpYG2YBJRtxt9T0Hdcc9PZzN7dojRbGrQjFwwOBxtqg9uPGa0tZq8fAJ4x8YIq4YIbeKUFtIyd2PBBrkVwS-oV-B1L9o4dJAmfDN_899e-3qwy7CXC0478CUyt5NrhQ973zzdW81qlGbHYGaruzGlt5xjx20QzRAuZIvIIOK1npfF5SH1tMIgcNh6R7TyvKms3w7dAAt5EjCqGgdnhnl2WMxMUBYjg9DYlkZRVlD5HI-j4qF_RoIZ84Uq3VjB7kkA/4qt/JgQLAAygSxGR5cNCmUR5Nw/h0/h001.Dmr4NxqJv-Dx7H9OOSFuDxE4U5Je3oc3R6iU5syQhBo)**.

We’re building a field program big enough to reach voters everywhere — at their doors, on their phones, in their neighborhoods, on video calls, at town halls, and through as many neighbor-to-neighbor conversations as possible.

Over the last few months, this campaign has:

• Knocked on 486,000 doors and called more than 300,000 voters
• Identified 154,000 supporters across San Francisco
• Participated in all 13 debates and forums offered in this race
• Hosted 21 neighborhood town halls, meet-and-greets, and rallies with more than 6,500 attendees
• Brought 1,300 voters onto 230 calls directly with Saikat
• Earned endorsements from 30 organizations from San Francisco and across the country
• Packed our Change the Party rally with more than 1,400 people at full capacity

These numbers give me such hope for our city and country. What started as a room of a few people planning to take on the establishment has turned into a movement of thousands in San Francisco — and across the nation — fighting to change the party.

We’re fighting because we know that San Francisco can and must lead the country again. We’re fighting because we believe this seat should belong to the people: not Super PAC backed, corporate-sponsored politicians, crypto billionaires, or the same, tired political establishment that got us here.

But rallies alone don’t win elections. Grassroots organizing does.

That is why our strategy is simple: we are going to keep talking to the voters who will decide this race, over and over, until Election Day. Recent polls show this race may come down to a field margin.

That’s good for us, because every time voters hear Saikat’s message — that we can lower costs, pass Medicare for All, ban congressional stock trading, take on corporate power, fully fund public transit, build affordable housing people, end U.S. involvement in needless wars, and stand up to Trump with courage — they break our way.

Right now, the single most important thing you can do is help us fuel this final push.

Every dollar we raise goes directly into reaching the voters who will decide whether Saikat makes it through the primary on June 2, and shows the establishment the true people power behind this campaign — through doors, phones, mail, digital, and the organizing program that is powering this campaign, we will reach every voter in SF.

If you can donate today, please do. And if you can volunteer, we need you too.
[Donate »](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqu9GgNqQBZQbHGys41Ff66GdRsXl3aU86FUQm8hkp73cI0TbF-sjuAc3AWQCrU7eDfzglP8k3hW99EItYQJJdhzbIncdJbUCGtFxIbE-07PyiJ-mUMnFVvn_1Wp1HfXJmq1Y1Q9hM161s8nnFPyoLrfIN4WA3HQtPgPqRrJ_4U-eRCl4XboMtuungJhkHsRELM4JVQRVptaiEZW7nU6TYmrZVH3dvLp8gMquVyoBB97spNjfrPwkFlApuB6EgKDdD3t6cPy5J324v7WDVAlwa67rzEd8h56ecRF4gI9aupg5xhVyS3Fw1tRPvbe2I5F_iMJFycRczAhxBDXp3lF_adjIUGxy1BhlxVkKO4E4JSJCg/4qt/JgQLAAygSxGR5cNCmUR5Nw/h1/h001.QzuatIZ97SHksD8sOoUX33UgEd-noSk2TLP11KF6ESY)[Sign up to volunteer »](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMe9suWVqtFb-BWoi2l0CARQ8xIrmPvasGsp-wbaBSFn3tI3OhSLfVTq7zYpdTXUTUdSWMTn9AHiTlpHZUZ9y-_xZ1JEWmGahTijWq5CyEgMSKD6ejAfbkv9eIjAt9NLycRWMTTH9_GnK_dDzC4yuzZJl-lMAz_JHtkSUTOXRenZlr07SRsnUbCHXBYLYMLn17_ArqeY2TTA1PBJaRXK2LqEoR_KzazU9iB7rJSdsngD2_u0DWO2aaBHAaqxcstpKSAW9pRwdrZzdBEc-7_-Ql3ah5v1QZ0GSJu8G7Iy_CnaarBVmVNK30RJvw5Fes9QcwA/4qt/JgQLAAygSxGR5cNCmUR5Nw/h2/h001.Lu2XhQ5PsAUTArp1HSiVr1WeUkwKbJHWlaAX9QjxYlc) Here’s what I know after almost a year on this campaign, in the trenches with Saikat, our organizers, and our incredible team of thousands of volunteers up close every day:

The energy is real. Our strategy is working. This race is ours to win or lose.

But the outcome is not automatic. It depends on whether we turn this momentum into votes, ballot by ballot and conversation by conversation.

For months, Saikat has been meeting voters directly — at town halls, on Zoom calls, at doors, at rallies, and in neighborhoods across San Francisco. He has made this campaign what politics should be: direct, honest, people-powered, and rooted in the belief that voters deserve more from their elected officials.

Now, we have less than 2 weeks to make sure every single person who is ready for new leadership knows exactly how to cast their vote and why this race matters.

Please donate today to help us scale this final push — or sign up to volunteer remotely and help us reach more voters before June 2.
[Chip in today »](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqu9GgNqQBZQbHGys41Ff66GdRsXl3aU86FUQm8hkp73cI0TbF-sjuAc3AWQCrU7eDdQg01vcij1KIIbj4B4avZV35-ar5L6guMJYBaNmISwz3UrifrESv9RzD1X-if8itXxO9mcpzUHFdT1qyznXo08JeoeRADVa30sPoTcrQ2NXCy84gAy99tpbkGsuaB9Z7h2ZW4DjoTN2WCtyEprpTM6r7w5V0fjgDqVHzJ3x4X3dXqyRtAfKob6I9mYX7EPdqaiqikDtNBOvDp9Pyw4_lBYJoRvb_hCo4hhZpC6J5rUNfC8kDQ__2a2WWLs8b3dfUebXZ2Pqj26gzwCHf8_WDxjk9ZG_33U9TWJN_QBiWasSg/4qt/JgQLAAygSxGR5cNCmUR5Nw/h3/h001.bkF-rgMhD0Lw0VnAwRl2SJJFKamRh8Vp8e14U8V7fQ4) [Volunteer remotely »](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMe9suWVqtFb-BWoi2l0CARQ8xIrmPvasGsp-wbaBSFn3tI3OhSLfVTq7zYpdTXUTUdsLY_LBNxj_VB7QgLuPtyOlpEnQO0Uhbb4qHhEpBdBcr9UefbBjA3Piu_AXHbk8kQuWHWcuJdVRCrqfWJeDXCZy2clteqJGqeuEK0oRXxu52SUw_WxSpqC7f-weW7RECyj5RtAAE-1wYToea24VD9TGMo7eEf52IiD9ebaTqm8HJYjWX123c6UhOlcCC44ureCDC0L8L6xzCw3RDEPmBooYVXjTh-NbcHbEHEYLP9Qy6ICuGyyRwNY4w1EVF6zoiw/4qt/JgQLAAygSxGR5cNCmUR5Nw/h4/h001.ksDlk3yI-NUg53EXQhjZnHZyFbkoKuoKoCbsDB6aCrc) When we win on June 2nd, we won’t just be laying the groundwork to send Saikat to Congress in November. We’ll be sending a message from San Francisco to the entire country: a different kind of Democratic Party is possible — and we’re building it right now.

Let’s win this thing,

-Emily

Emily Hyden
Campaign Manager
Saikat for Congress

clean_body: Rallies alone don’t win elections. Grassroots organizing does. | | | | Hi folks, This is Emily, Saikat’s campaign manager. The primary is on June 2nd, less than two weeks away, so I thought it’d be a good time for us to pull back the curtain on where things stand. You can help us sprint through the finish line by . We’re building a field program big enough to reach voters everywhere — at their doors, on their phones, in their neighborhoods, on video calls, at town halls, and through as many neighbor-to-neighbor conversations as possible. Over the last few months, this campaign has: • Knocked on 486,000 doors and called more than 300,000 voters • Identified 154,000 supporters across San Francisco • Participated in all 13 debates and forums offered in this race • Hosted 21 neighborhood town halls, meet-and-greets, and rallies with more than 6,500 attendees • Brought 1,300 voters onto 230 calls directly with Saikat • Earned endorsements from 30 organizations from San Francisco and across the country • Packed our Change the Party rally with more than 1,400 people at full capacity These numbers give me such hope for our city and country. What started as a room of a few people planning to take on the establishment has turned into a movement of thousands in San Francisco — and across the nation — fighting to change the party. We’re fighting because we know that San Francisco can and must lead the country again. We’re fighting because we believe this seat should belong to the people: not Super PAC backed, corporate-sponsored politicians, crypto billionaires, or the same, tired political establishment that got us here. But rallies alone don’t win elections. Grassroots organizing does. That is why our strategy is simple: we are going to keep talking to the voters who will decide this race, over and over, until Election Day. Recent polls show this race may come down to a field margin. That’s good for us, because every time voters hear Saikat’s message — that we can lower costs, pass Medicare for All, ban congressional stock trading, take on corporate power, fully fund public transit, build affordable housing people, end U.S. involvement in needless wars, and stand up to Trump with courage — they break our way. Right now, the single most important thing you can do is help us fuel this final push. Every dollar we raise goes directly into reaching the voters who will decide whether Saikat makes it through the primary on June 2, and shows the establishment the true people power behind this campaign — through doors, phones, mail, digital, and the organizing program that is powering this campaign, we will reach every voter in SF. If you can donate today, please do. And if you can volunteer, we need you too. Here’s what I know after almost a year on this campaign, in the trenches with Saikat, our organizers, and our incredible team of thousands of volunteers up close every day: The energy is real. Our strategy is working. This race is ours to win or lose. But the outcome is not automatic. It depends on whether we turn this momentum into votes, ballot by ballot and conversation by conversation. For months, Saikat has been meeting voters directly — at town halls, on Zoom calls, at doors, at rallies, and in neighborhoods across San Francisco. He has made this campaign what politics should be: direct, honest, people-powered, and rooted in the belief that voters deserve more from their elected officials. Now, we have less than 2 weeks to make sure every single person who is ready for new leadership knows exactly how to cast their vote and why this race matters. Please donate today to help us scale this final push — or sign up to volunteer remotely and help us reach more voters before June 2. When we win on June 2nd, we won’t just be laying the groundwork to send Saikat to Congress in November. We’ll be sending a message from San Francisco to the entire country: a different kind of Democratic Party is possible — and we’re building it right now. Donald Trump ran on fiscal responsibility. He promised to drain the swamp, cut waste, and put Americans first. But the latest headlines tell a very different story – one of breathtaking self-dealing at our expense:

Now he's negotiated a settlement that could create a $1.8 billion taxpayer-funded "weaponization compensation fund" – with no transparency or oversight requirements – that could be used to reward political allies, including J6 insurrectionists and white supremacists.
And new reports show that in the first quarter of this year, [Trump made more than 3,600 stock trades](https://us.list-manage.com/wxjyDx5lWPW?e=395a33a3d2&c2id=2ea96fa4e6b867a41c995b28450e35c7) involving companies whose profits have been directly impacted by his decisions as president.
This is not fiscal conservatism. This is kleptocracy.

It’s no wonder that Trump said he doesn’t think much about the financial well-being of Americans. I am OUTRAGED, and I will not stay silent. I hope you won’t either.

And after more than a decade of Abbott, we are ranking near the bottom on the things families actually care about: Too many Texans and Texas kids still don’t have health insurance or coverage Utility bills keep going up Gas and groceries are way too expensive Public schools are losing funding while private voucher schemes get pushed through Abbott wants to campaign on the state’s prosperity, but that couldn’t be further from the truth — way too many families are living a different reality than the one he’s bragging about. And now that this race is tightening, Abbott is going to do what he always does when he feels threatened. He’s going to lean on his billionaire donors, flood the airwaves, and try to distract Texans instead of earning their votes. That’s why what we do right now matters. Over the past few weeks, there have been clear warning signs that the Left is stepping up its efforts to gain ground in communities across our state. And they’re treating local races as the first step in a much larger strategy.

We’re seeing it play out in real time: well-funded Democratic campaigns, national money flowing into local contests, and coordinated messaging designed to flip long-held Republican areas.

And they believe momentum is building.....

Here’s what this broader pattern looks like right now:

* **Across Florida:** Democrats are investing heavily in local and municipal races they previously ignored.
* **Nationally:** The Left continues pushing candidates and policies focused on open borders, higher taxes, and expanded government control.
* **In major cities:** Progressive leadership is doubling down on policies that have led to rising costs, strained services, and public safety concerns.

Florida Democrats and their allies are framing these local gains as proof that the political landscape is shifting — _**and they’re openly signaling that the midterms are their next target.**_

We’re seeing it play out in real time: well-funded Democratic campaigns, national money flowing into local contests, and coordinated messaging designed to flip long-held Republican areas. And they believe momentum is building..... Here’s what this broader pattern looks like right now: Across Florida: Democrats are investing heavily in local and municipal races they previously ignored. Nationally: The Left continues pushing candidates and policies focused on open borders, higher taxes, and expanded government control. In major cities: Progressive leadership is doubling down on policies that have led to rising costs, strained services, and public safety concerns. Florida Democrats and their allies are framing these local gains as proof that the political landscape is shifting — and they’re openly signaling that the midterms are their next target. Out-of-state money is already flowing into Florida at scale, and national organizations are treating our state as one of the top battlegrounds in the country. _Joe Sokol Contributed to this Article._
A Bangor dog owner is facing civil charges after his pit bull reportedly charged aggressively toward his neighbor's three-year-old on Tuesday, and the neighbor fatally shot the dog.
[RELATED: [Bangor Man Arrested for Stealing a Woman's Hat and Pushing Her Out of Her Wheelchair...](https://substack.com/redirect/4a56f3cd-c18c-49b4-b1be-5764ef163488?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)]
At approximately 8:48 a.m., the Bangor Police Department received a report of shots fired on March Street.
Officers responded and allegedly found that a resident of March Street had fired at and struck a large dog after it charged at him and his toddlers.
Adam Stade, the man who shot the pit bull named "Blink," spoke with the Maine Wire and explained his side of the story.
"If you are a dog owner, you still have a responsibility to protect other little kids and grown-ups from your dog, and it's sad that there are so many irresponsible dog owners out there," said Stade.
He told us that the shooting was not the first time he had been menaced by the animal.
The first incident took place the same week the shooting happened.
Stade said that he previously called police following one of the incidents, and Animal Control responded. They allegedly attempted to speak with the dog's owner, who he says refused to open his door for them and only spoke with them through his window.
After animal control spoke with the owner, the dog was allowed off leash again, and the owner reportedly claimed that his animal would never hurt anyone, according to Stade.
"You need to put your dog on a leash; if he comes over here, I will shoot your dog. I don't want to shoot anyone's dog; I love dogs, but I don't want that dog attacking me or my son," warned Stade.
Stade says he believes the dog's owner let go of its collar on purpose before it charged at him. He also said that he often hears screaming from the dog owner's house.
"That dog came flying straight across his whole driveway into my yard, and I shot it with Benny [Stade's son] right behind me. I shot at it four times and hit it once, then the kid came flying over my garden to get his dog and chased it back to his place," Stade told The Maine Wire.
"My main thought was, 'Benny's right here; I can't let the dog get past me,'" he added.
Stade said that after the incident, he began getting death threats online. He provided a screenshot of some of the messages he received from a Facebook user by the name Reegan Katherine, who appeared to explicitly threaten to murder Stade and wish death upon his son.
Stade said that he showed Katherine's threat to police, who have, he says, issued a summons to Katherine for allegedly issuing a threat.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7e32a63c-aae7-45d7-a2e6-cede7901d4ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

"Nothing in the news coverage of it said that it was a father, a single dad of a three-year-old protecting his son from a vicious pitbull that was attacking him on his property, so it's a lot of media bias," said Stade.
He said that people posted his business card online including his phone number and email address.
He blamed WABI-TV's coverage of the incident for the death threats and hate he received.
Stade praised the police response to the incident.
"I love all those people down there," said Stade. "They're all really great people."
He was given his handgun back on Wednesday, the day after the incident.
According to police, the dog was initially transported to an emergency veterinarian by the Bangor Animal Control Officer.
Detectives began an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident, including a review of video footage of the alleged shooting.
Following the investigation, detectives allegedly determined that Stade and his toddler were playing outside in a small area of their driveway at the time.
At the same time, the neighbor's dog was not tethered or under the control of its owner, and allegedly ran aggressively towards the Stade and his son.
On Wednesday, the dog's owner was charged with dogs at large, a civil offense.
The owner had reportedly been warned by animal control officers previously for failing to control the dog.
The owner of the dog, identified by the [Bangor Daily News](https://substack.com/redirect/8f4bdb49-dabf-408e-889a-eacb8b6bc430?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as Samuel Robichaud, spoke with the outlet and identified the dog as a Pitbull, and said that it was put down due to the severity of its injuries.
Adam shared the security footage with the Maine Wire and sat down with us for an interview.

## **Wall Street is hiding a $3 trillion secret.**
It's a shadow banking system that operates in the dark. Worse?
Over 40% of these corporate borrowers are already bleeding cash.
Even JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon is sounding the alarm, warning that lenders are doing "dumb things" and the parallels to 2008 are hard to ignore.
And it could be sitting **[right inside your retirement account.](https://substack.com/redirect/eb76b588-3b42-43e2-9c5e-b4eddcecb273?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

* * *
_**(Piece continues below)**_
"It was gross. I don't find those jokes to be funny -- jokes about lynching Black people. Lynching is not a joke. That's worse than rape. You're not joking about rape, are you?...You know you can't do that, but you can say 'lynching'?" Handler asked.
"If [Underwood] says she's fine with that, she's fine with that," Handler begrudgingly acknowledged. "I wasn't fine with that. I thought that was disgusting, too."
Underwood **[recently went on Gillis' podcast](https://substack.com/redirect/85009626-de8d-494c-9e9f-b602adafc32c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to reaffirm that she was not offended by the jokes about her husband.
It is not surprising Handler, fresh off of telling voters in Los Angeles to not vote for Spencer Pratt for mayor, found many of the jokes offensive. What is surprising is how Handler does not seem to understand what a roast entails. The whole reason why they are such big events is because it is a rare, no hold barred joking session.

I want you to meet Clarissa, our lead organizer in the Rio Grande Valley.
She has been organizing with Powered by People since 2024. In fact she started out as a volunteer, someone whose hustle and ability to connect with young future voters made an impression on me when I first met her in McAllen more than two years ago.
She has brought that determination and power of connection to the job. She is responsible for recruiting and leading volunteers, finding promising locations for us to meet and register voters, and keeping up the spirits of her team in a part of the state that doesn’t get enough of the love and attention that typically flows to places like Austin, Dallas and Houston.

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

Dear Friend,

Imagine this: It's a dark night in Newark, New Jersey. A young officer, just 26 years old, father of four, races to back up his brothers in blue. A dangerous chase unfolds – armed thugs in a speeding car, weaving through streets at 70 mph the wrong way, endangering innocent families. These criminals point a loaded semi-automatic right at Officer Jovanny Crespo's face. They try to mow him down like roadkill. In a split-second decision, the kind no desk-jockey prosecutor could ever understand, Officer Crespo acts to protect himself, his fellow officers, and the public. He stops the threat. Lives are saved. But what does he get in return? Handcuffs. Indictment. A sham trial where he's branded a "murderer" and "killer" by radicals who hate the badge. | [Help Free JOVANNY](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=69a2b9366c484fec845b35776b51afec&_e=ZkZUpqbZtEf53c3_KJihqeiODqIkruLWxR4xoqGWsqaKbiDcUuHw-a0l5jGaP12mJPD-YCWT13AhzuJZ3CHzBv1LeK_BhelWOYbkNzLeilxAMMD1kbGH2YIHKKzcTgnFPOKY-U6EJoiLVKlq_1JMCp6rZJyvJM8havAYpLaJR9uEtN9ohEWXqNIp6l30jprz9CP0Z19uDt8hVK0dHRkJx2qnoejX2ddq_j1Es507vnQ_eCTQ-RnVMe8WshFM_R2Ss_Yf5jsur0Dlg0yHMQ9X00b0kZZgdjY6OYDy1XNmPeCm-4oPP6GCQlKXuBbR3euWs25kIAw-XRD8Opqf4p73bYZDcz8h8WQ_Q4XJtO3cz4SWG5Q10JdSqhT5uW4Jk73L_9p88slo2G1UtTgkRqMUcrr1SAmaCw1yUHaxS13xk9wU4SjoTS5sCrxV-T3aq-85)

**By Eric Lullove, DPM, CWSP, MAPWCA, FFPM RCPS(Glasg)**
_Chief executive and medical officer, West Boca Center for Wound Healing, Coconut Creek, Florida | Contributing medical editor, Blue Amp Media_
* * *
I want you to picture someone. Let's call her Margaret. She's 67. She's a retired schoolteacher from central Florida--the kind of woman who packed lunches every morning for thirty years without complaint and never once called in sick. She found a lump. She found it in the shower on a Tuesday morning in November, and now she's sitting in my colleague's office, terrified, being told that the clinical trial she qualified for--the one that might have given her a real fighting chance against a particularly aggressive form of breast cancer--has been shut down.
Not because the science didn't work. Not because the drug failed. Because the funding was pulled. Because someone in Washington decided the National Institutes of Health needed to be trimmed like fat off a spreadsheet.
Margaret isn't a hypothetical. She is every patient I've ever known. She is your mother. She might be you.
And I think it's time we had a real conversation about what that actually costs--not in policy language or budget jargon, but in real, human terms. In dollars and years and the quiet devastation of diseases that didn't have to get this bad.
#### _We are not cutting "government waste." We are cutting the pipeline between a scientist's breakthrough and your survival. Those are not the same thing._
## Let's Start with the Numbers
I'll be upfront: numbers alone don't move people. But context does. So let me give you both.
In the first three months of 2025 alone, the Trump administration effectively cut **$2.7 billion in NIH funding** , terminating more than 3,200 research grants compared to the same period the year before. [1] That's not a proposal on a whiteboard. That already happened. Those dollars are gone. And the consequences are only now beginning to surface.
And then there's what's proposed for next year. The FY2026 White House budget called for a **40% cut --an $18 billion reduction**--that would push NIH to the lowest inflation-adjusted funding level in 25 years. [3] Congress pushed back hard on the full cut, but the damage already done in 2025 is real and not reversible with a press release.
Sit with that phrase: the lowest level in 25 years. While the diseases we're fighting--the cancers, the dementias, the diabetic complications that fill my wound care clinic every day--have only gotten more complex, more expensive, and more prevalent. The math here is not complicated. The consequences are not distant. They are already arriving.
## A Wound Care Doctor's Honest Assessment
I've spent more than twenty years standing over wounds--wounds that should never have gotten this bad, that represent years of undertreated disease, financial stress, and delayed care. And there's something I tell my residents, something that sounds almost too simple, but that I've never once seen disproved in clinical practice: _the most expensive patient is the one who didn 't get help six months ago._
That's what NIH cuts do at a systemic level. They are the policy equivalent of ignoring an infection until it becomes sepsis. You close your eyes, call it "efficiency," rename the agencies--and for a while, nothing looks visibly different. The labs are still lit. The researchers still show up. The patients in the trials still get their infusions.
And then, one by one, the lights go out.
Former NIH Director Dr. Francis Collins--the man who helped lead the Human Genome Project, who served under three presidents--put it plainly: "When you're talking about medical research, when you're talking about people's lives, when you're talking about clinical trials for Alzheimer's or cancer that may take three or four years, you can't just go in and decide, 'I'm going to shut those down and maybe I'll try something else.' Those are people's lives at risk." [4]
He also made the return-on-investment case that should appeal to anyone who balks at the cost of science: every dollar the NIH invested in 2024 returned $2.56 in economic activity within the year. [5] Over the past decade, NIH funding has driven more than $822 billion in new economic activity and supported 3.7 million jobs. [5]
So when someone tells you cutting NIH saves money--with the most respectful version of physician directness I can muster--they are wrong. It doesn't save money. It defers it. It transfers it. It multiplies it. And it drops it on you.
#### _In wound care, we say: "Dead tissue doesn't heal." You cannot revive a research program with a press release after you've let it bleed out. And you cannot undo the science that never happened._
## The Hidden Tax on Your Family
Here's what this means to you personally--not as a citizen, but as someone who has a body, a family, and a future medical bill you haven't gotten yet.
Let me walk you through one disease--Alzheimer's--because it illustrates what happens when research stalls and care costs compound.
Alzheimer's and related dementias are projected to cost the U.S. health care system **$409 billion in 2026 alone**. That's direct health and long-term care--not counting the $446 billion in unpaid family caregiving hours provided by nearly 13 million Americans who quit jobs, defer their own health care, and exhaust their savings to keep a loved one alive and dignified. [7] By 2050, total care costs are projected to reach nearly $1 trillion per year. [7]
The National Institute on Aging--where Alzheimer's and dementia research lives--is facing a proposed **45.5% cut** in grant funding and a **24.5% reduction** in research center support. [3]
We were getting closer to something real. Disease-modifying therapies. Earlier detection. Drugs that might actually slow the disease--not just manage the symptoms. And now those labs are dark, those researchers are updating their resumes, and the cost of care will keep climbing while the pipeline of solutions runs dry.
The same math plays out in cancer. In diabetes. In heart disease--a disease where, because of NIH-funded research over decades, deaths have dropped by roughly 75%. [4] That progress didn't happen automatically. It happened because a generation of scientists, funded year after year by the NIH, showed up and did the work. Gut the funding, and the next generation of progress doesn't happen. It's that direct.
## Who Pays When the Research Stops?
You do. Your family does. That's the honest answer, and I think you deserve to hear it plainly.
When a disease that could have been caught in stage I is caught in stage IV instead, the cost difference isn't marginal. For breast cancer, early-stage treatment costs roughly $60,000 to $100,000. Late-stage metastatic treatment can exceed $300,000 per patient--before accounting for home health care, lost income, and the family members who have to leave work to become full-time caregivers.
When we defund research, we don't save money. We finance a catastrophe on an installment plan--with the payments pushed far enough into the future that the people who made this decision won't be in office when the bill comes due. But you will be. Your kids will be.
This is also a workforce story that doesn't get told enough. Every canceled NIH grant isn't just a failed experiment. It's a researcher who spent eight years in training--who chose this path because they believed that figuring out why cells go wrong matters more than a bigger paycheck--now applying for jobs in Europe or leaving science entirely. You can't pause a scientific career and pick it up three years later. That institutional knowledge, those research networks, those methodologies honed over decades--they scatter. They don't come back on demand.
#### _This isn 't fiscal responsibility. This is fiscal cowardice dressed up as reform. And the invoice is already being written--in your name._
## Clinical Trials Aren't Light Switches
I want to come back to those 74,000 people in interrupted trials, because I don't think that number lands the way it should.
Seventy-four thousand people. That's not a statistic. That's a stadium full of people who volunteered--who signed consent forms and showed up for appointments and, in some cases, let researchers implant devices or give them experimental drugs--because they believed the research mattered. They trusted the system.
Dr. Vishal Patel of Brigham and Women's Hospital, who led the _**JAMA Internal Medicine**_ study, put it clearly: "If you pause an experiment, especially when it comes to experiments involving drugs and patients where you need a consistent dose over time and consistent measurements, it's possible that you just screwed up the entire research." [8]
Some of those patients lost access to their medication. Some were left with unmonitored implants. Some participated in trials whose results will now never be published. And the researchers at the Rhode Island Public Health Institute? "I panicked," said Dr. Amy Nunn, a professor at Brown University School of Public Health. "I was worried we might lose everything." [8]
The knowledge that those 383 trials would have generated--about what works and what doesn't, about how to improve population health, about how to catch disease earlier and treat it better--that knowledge is gone. As Dr. Nunn said: "The knowledge that we would have had about how we can enhance population health through those clinical trials will be lost." [8]
That's the part that keeps me up at night. Not just the people in those trials today, but the ones in twenty years who won't have a treatment--because the research that should have produced it was shut down in 2025.
## What You Can Actually Do
_A practical plan --because outrage without direction doesn't heal anything._
I don't write pieces like this to leave you sitting in helpless anger. That's not medicine. That's not useful. So let me give you something concrete--real steps, real tools, real ways to push back in your own life and community. Some of these take five minutes. Some take more. All of them matter.
### 1\. Know What's at Stake in Your State
NIH funding doesn't just live in Bethesda, Maryland. It flows to universities, research hospitals, and medical centers in every congressional district in the country. The United for Medical Research tool at unitedformedicalresearch.org lets you look up exactly how much NIH funding your state receives and how many jobs it supports. When you call your congressman, this number is the most powerful sentence you can say: "NIH funding supports X jobs and $X million in our district--and you're voting to cut it."
### 2\. Call--Not Email--Your Representatives
Emails get logged and ignored. Phone calls get counted and reported. Call both of your U.S. senators and your House member. Find their numbers at congress.gov/members/find-your-member. Keep it simple: "I'm a constituent. I'm calling because I'm concerned about cuts to NIH research. I want my representative to oppose any reduction in NIH funding in the FY2026 and FY2027 budgets." Congressional offices track these calls by issue. Volume moves votes.
### 3\. Support the Organizations Fighting This Every Day
Several organizations are doing the legal and legislative heavy lifting right now. The American Association for Cancer Research (aacr.org) is actively rallying researchers and patients. Research!America (researchamerica.org) tracks legislation and issues action alerts. The Alzheimer's Association (alz.org) has an advocacy center specifically for this fight. Even a $25 annual membership or a single constituent letter makes these organizations stronger when they lobby on your behalf.
### 4\. Talk to Your Doctor--and Ask Them to Speak Up Too
Physicians carry enormous credibility with legislators, and most of us have professional associations that lobby on our behalf. But our professional associations need to hear from patients too. If your doctor has mentioned cuts to research funding, ask them if their specialty society is advocating against it. If you're a patient who has benefited from a clinical trial, that story is more powerful than any policy document. The American Medical Association (ama-assn.org) has policy portals where patient voices can be formally submitted.
### 5\. Share This Story--Especially with People Who Don't Think It Affects Them
The most effective thing you can do right now, today, in the next five minutes, is forward this article to someone who votes but doesn't follow health policy. The people who think NIH funding is an abstraction for scientists--not something that touches their families--are the most important audience for this conversation. Write one sentence: "This is about your family's future medical bills and treatments that won't exist. Worth five minutes." That's the whole ask.
### 6\. If You're a Researcher, Don't Go Quietly
If you work in biomedical research and your grant has been disrupted or threatened, document everything and connect with the American Association of University Professors (aaup.org) and the Association of American Universities (aau.edu). Both are tracking the legal landscape and supporting researchers navigating terminations. You have rights. Use them. And if you're considering leaving the country for a research position, I understand--but the field will be worse for losing you, and so will the patients who depend on what you're building.
## One More Thing
I'm a wound care physician. I walk into a clinic every day and look at what happens to a body when something that should have been addressed early was left to worsen. The wound gets bigger. The infection goes deeper. What was once a conversation becomes a surgery. What was once a surgery becomes an amputation.
I have watched people lose limbs to the compounding consequences of neglected care. And I am watching this country do the exact same thing to its own medical research infrastructure--and calling it responsible governance.
It isn't. It is reckless. It is a slow amputation performed without anesthesia on the organ that keeps this nation medically alive.
But here's what I know from twenty-plus years of doing this: wounds, even serious ones, can heal. Not always perfectly. Not without scar tissue. But they can heal--when they're treated with urgency, skill, and the right resources.
The research infrastructure of this country is not beyond saving. But the window is not infinite. The scientists we lose today don't come back. The trials that ended in 2025 don't restart in 2027. The cures that weren't developed won't appear on their own.
This is the moment for urgency. Not panic--urgency. There is a difference. Panic is paralyzing. Urgency moves people from their chairs to their phones, from their phones to their representatives, and from their representatives to something that might actually change.
**Make some noise. Margaret is depending on it.**

subject: Native Nonprofit Day: Why Indigenous-Led Organizations Matter More Than Ever
body:
Indigenous communities hold the solutions — help ensure they are resourced to thrive. Native-led nonprofits receive less than 1% of charitable giving. Help us change that. | | | **Dear Friends and Relatives,** I wanted to send a quick note about a few things: take time for yourself, you are doing good work, but in this moment in time, where chaos is happening, just take time and rest. Secondly, I just want to say thank Mother Nature for creating conditions that are letting some of us in North Carolina feel some rain upon the earth. Finally, today is **[Native Nonprofit Day:](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_ZQqlt19aM_Mpt4TRcI5Xl_8w-17OXMy365yZDmi0YKkk7yFe1-FO0XlNzoHU5Xor-o1Fj_CQvzqBaOW26SkWMl5knkCQHeOax39WZAOz21cAIXEgh6ClhvFkb5ylfoQGvuGLV0aSYzTCudo5IC_3e6UX4DecHTCpERde-0MIlKEqk2jkbDoWc0FJ1fjSL3-kIumVHlEORMxUd5AhDdYHtDjShb9QlkZnK6N-W6PM51ZZ0nNXUdMRGs141nLKFdGxLGJU-4IBrHSnq-iacbWeW2dOr__aVJZcsdX6aVAhFjJQdboGQXau2GLdU1t-Fa5Du90U9odEd6-KKgav4jeCck_rBxhO7WBgQRDlOnjbVMsCh_iOH-KQllJP6GavU7DQH5Y1AAxuFRQLSa22KQf_oZkb5heiPDgD90Vy2GBdPe2OswtBS91oFHn0px-Vylyg/4qt/dWCbEt2dRLyFl1n37YgnGQ/h0/h001.GC7zDBHop4w0zqlBfCVCTvXFwGm-9ucdh7d_vlWtaKI) Why Indigenous-Led Organizations Matter More Than Ever. **There are days when the weight of this work feels overwhelming. The political climate. The constant attacks on our communities, our waters, our rights, and our futures. The exhaustion that comes from organizing against pipelines, data centers, environmental destruction, and systems that continue to place profit over people. The eco-grief of watching forests be cleared, rivers be threatened, and communities be sacrificed while trying to hold space for hope at the same time. Many of us in movement spaces are carrying deep fatigue right now. And yet — Indigenous communities continue to rise. Today is Native Nonprofit Day, and it exists because Native-led organizations continue to do transformative work despite being among the most underfunded in the country. Native-led organizations hold community knowledge. We understand the histories, relationships, responsibilities, and realities our communities face because we live them ourselves. We know that protecting water is tied to protecting culture. We know that healing communities require land, language, food, ceremony, and belonging. We know that environmental justice cannot exist without Indigenous sovereignty and leadership. At 7 Directions of Service, this work happens every single day. We organize against fossil fuel expansion projects like MVP Southgate and the Southeast Supply Enhancement Project. We work alongside frontline communities fighting environmental injustice across North Carolina. We advocate for the rights of Nature and the protection of sacred places. We create youth programs rooted in culture and land-based learning. We grow food and community at YESA Farm. We hold space for healing, storytelling, and Indigenous futures. But the truth is, this work is often carried out with very limited resources. Native communities face some of the highest rates of inequality in the United States, yet Native-led nonprofits receive less than 1% of all charitable giving nationwide. Less than 1%. That means many Indigenous-led organizations are expected to respond to crises, organize communities, support families, protect land and water, preserve culture, educate youth, and build long-term solutions while [operating](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_ZQqlt19aM_Mpt4TRcI5Xl_8w-17OXMy365yZDmi0YKkk7yFe1-FO0XlNzoHU5Xor-o1Fj_CQvzqBaOW26SkWMa2pPVPlr34YgGYhZn2zJrNUltb3Z1hvw9xOWdh0jqglD0H0VDstDyqCwEE8KThsyQnQf36_4VpY1-Yr1yodeLI8zUQBk74trS_JWvRbqCocQSQ-xb2g4I4IoHRU_idcpzqISRleX3ZMiqUzGy4VYxpYse53UFBO2ee99DZRJL-HD3f3_cskNprog-vn_aWud6vJ583sLU8tRaed2Ymc-6DopwkzR6w5p_dAsliKYNouSiqO4YU7US-rgu0FhLn2GauasoNpjioc70lYRzsW2WNv4Utt14NmOFc9xIic7GpKoGZ_cKF5_K5ItmLwDOu54sm2ykdkHWBnvxaPaXY9548JfzcUOPced6uaKSTyENhw/4qt/dWCbEt2dRLyFl1n37YgnGQ/h1/h001.xCF7tmSW2if4G_J1T5WAbJrpy0_aFe8XaGNgSVeRi28) with a fraction of the support available to larger institutions. Still, we continue. Not because it is easy.
Not because we are not tired.
But because our communities, ancestors, and future generations matter. In moments like these, [sustaining](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_ZQqlt19aM_Mpt4TRcI5Xl_8w-17OXMy365yZDmi0YKkk7yFe1-FO0XlNzoHU5Xor-o1Fj_CQvzqBaOW26SkWMjOND0ncjycBn-H7gz0_1NlzVoZsAxLRb7GyVUuSXfYSSSzsxbSHiIJp4GYn1DK7pLMvw2oFdzgtrHWhcGjmFWvkI88oT1SCuNW2NSyv1Qq50BW_oh-8b6paddx_H18SMnloroxzYU2_Pw52me1zs1EIXua2vMRZiSa3qcpPe_QV1D9bIMRkD2-ZZz4AYqbHW07MajddzzUHFDWsDtMYJ0oJ2FRaaYSuQwFqN-NPGU8Q_ZJGmHoV4wfyn5cFKt6HEfMLx83EtfOIsjL389EKFdk6VvjW-S3_eohWbztpyaQdnWZ-LWuTGKyOp9PbW9c2VEwXUK-fDNIxZ6xupX6PK7c_Xl_FDKcGrg8XvKaTOufc/4qt/dWCbEt2dRLyFl1n37YgnGQ/h2/h001.tw88InhPOvoSHeoKVOsH0L5-ym8odi2EDUO8aXZTYu0) support matters deeply. Monthly giving helps organizations like 7 Directions of Service continue responding to urgent threats while also building long-term Indigenous-led solutions rooted in justice, cultural revitalization, environmental stewardship, and collective care. A recurring gift helps support:

1. Indigenous environmental justice organizing
2. Resistance to harmful fossil fuel expansion
3. Rights of Nature advocacy
4. Youth leadership and cultural revitalization
5. Food sovereignty and YESA Farm programs
6. Community healing and mutual ai
