clean_body: Indigenous communities hold the solutions — help ensure they are resourced to thrive. Native-led nonprofits receive less than 1% of charitable giving. Help us change that. | | | Dear Friends and Relatives, I wanted to send a quick note about a few things: take time for yourself, you are doing good work, but in this moment in time, where chaos is happening, just take time and rest. Secondly, I just want to say thank Mother Nature for creating conditions that are letting some of us in North Carolina feel some rain upon the earth. Finally, today is Why Indigenous-Led Organizations Matter More Than Ever. There are days when the weight of this work feels overwhelming. The political climate. The constant attacks on our communities, our waters, our rights, and our futures. The exhaustion that comes from organizing against pipelines, data centers, environmental destruction, and systems that continue to place profit over people. The eco-grief of watching forests be cleared, rivers be threatened, and communities be sacrificed while trying to hold space for hope at the same time. Many of us in movement spaces are carrying deep fatigue right now. And yet — Indigenous communities continue to rise. Today is Native Nonprofit Day, and it exists because Native-led organizations continue to do transformative work despite being among the most underfunded in the country. Native-led organizations hold community knowledge. We understand the histories, relationships, responsibilities, and realities our communities face because we live them ourselves. We know that protecting water is tied to protecting culture. We know that healing communities require land, language, food, ceremony, and belonging. We know that environmental justice cannot exist without Indigenous sovereignty and leadership. At 7 Directions of Service, this work happens every single day. We organize against fossil fuel expansion projects like MVP Southgate and the Southeast Supply Enhancement Project. We work alongside frontline communities fighting environmental injustice across North Carolina. We advocate for the rights of Nature and the protection of sacred places. We create youth programs rooted in culture and land-based learning. We grow food and community at YESA Farm. We hold space for healing, storytelling, and Indigenous futures. But the truth is, this work is often carried out with very limited resources. Native communities face some of the highest rates of inequality in the United States, yet Native-led nonprofits receive less than 1% of all charitable giving nationwide. Less than 1%. That means many Indigenous-led organizations are expected to respond to crises, organize communities, support families, protect land and water, preserve culture, educate youth, and build long-term solutions while with a fraction of the support available to larger institutions. Still, we continue. Not because it is easy. Not because we are not tired. But because our communities, ancestors, and future generations matter. In moments like these, support matters deeply. Monthly giving helps organizations like 7 Directions of Service continue responding to urgent threats while also building long-term Indigenous-led solutions rooted in justice, cultural revitalization, environmental stewardship, and collective care. A recurring gift helps support: 1. Indigenous environmental justice organizing 2. Resistance to harmful fossil fuel expansion 3. Rights of Nature advocacy 4. Youth leadership and cultural revitalization 5. Food sovereignty and YESA Farm programs 6. Community healing and mutual ai 7. Protection of sacred lands and waters Whether it is $5, $10, or $25 helps sustain Indigenous-led work at a time when these efforts are urgently needed. name: AOC
subject: To working people, "earn" means something
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
Jeff Bezos' newspaper — The Washington Post — was not happy that I recently discussed how billionaires don't "earn" their wealth, they abuse market power to amass wealth while millions of Americans bear the cost.
There aren't a lot of billionaires in an absolute sense, but the proportion of billionaires that are upset with my comments are quite high.
**To a working person, and to working people, "earn" means something** : the calluses on your hands, the aches in your joints, the way we put ourselves through school with our first job.
I think that we are in an "emperor with no clothes" moment when it comes to the American economy and our democracy.
The Virginia redistricting maps were just overturned by judges that are largely financed by a movement of billionaires.
American inequality is at an absolute peak. **We have to ask ourselves if this is how we want to live as a society — if we want 3,400 billionaires to be prioritized over more than 300 million people**.
When we question the legitimacy of that power structure, the people at the top are going to be very mad.
Jeff Bezos purchased The Washington Post, he laid off some of the highest-qualified journalists that made it an American institution, so that he could turn it into a mouthpiece that launders his personal agenda and opinions.
He then uses this mouthpiece to take aim at politicians that want to question the deeply unequal and unjust distribution of power in America.
They want to continue to threaten and undercut those who say that democracy belongs at the ballot box — and that economic and political power should belong with the people of this country, not the very few.
**But together, we’ve built a movement fighting _against_ entrenched power and _for_ transformative change**, from Medicare for All to democratizing fundraising power in politics.

In solidarity,
Alexandria

name: Matt Ortega
subject: Getting our message out in the home stretch
body:
We don't have the budget for TV ads so we're reaching voters in other ways. | | | Friend, we are in the home stretch with less than two weeks to go until the June 2 primary. The latest data shows only 1,724 early voting ballots for this district have been returned. California's 14th District voters are still deciding who to support. A few weeks ago, one of our opponents refused to explain why she had contributed to the campaigns of far-right extremists like Laura Loomer. She sought to glibly deflect a clearly damaging truth about her past by stating, "let's leave it to the voters." **Okay then. Challenge accepted.** We had a special batch of campaign yard signs produced to inform voters of Rakhi Israni's documented history of financially supporting far-right extremists—and we are placing them next to hers wherever they are found in public spaces all across the district.

body:
Young Americans have always believed the future would offer more opportunity than the past. That optimism has long been one of the country’s defining strengths. But new polling suggests that confidence is starting to crack and policymakers should pay attention.

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
Young Americans have always believed the future would offer more opportunity than the past. That optimism has long been one of the country’s defining strengths. But new polling suggests that confidence is starting to crack and policymakers should pay attention.

A recent Gallup survey found that just 43% of Americans ages 15 to 34 believe now is a good time to find a job where they live, a stunning reversal from historic trends. It's not surprising. They are entering adulthood during a period of economic whiplash: pandemic disruption, inflation, housing costs that feel permanently out of reach, rising student debt, and growing uncertainty around artificial intelligence and the future of white-collar work. Axios recently reported that unemployment among recent college graduates has climbed above the national average and underemployment remains high.

Many did what society told them to do: work hard, get educated, build skills, and prepare for the future. Now, too many feel like they are walking into a system that no longer guarantees stability, affordability, or even a clear path forward. That frustration is real. But it is also a warning sign for a country that depends on innovation, entrepreneurship, and upward mobility to thrive.

The answer cannot simply be nostalgia for an older economy that is not coming back. AI is real. Automation is real. Global competition is real. The world is changing quickly, whether our political system is prepared for it or not.

That is where the Forward Party believes a different kind of politics matters.

Forward’s approach starts with a simple idea: government should focus less on ideological warfare and more on helping people successfully navigate a changing future. That means investing in workforce development, apprenticeships, modern career training, entrepreneurship, technical education, and AI literacy. It means preparing students not just for the jobs that existed 20 years ago, but for the industries and technologies that will define the next 20\. It also means recognizing that dignity and purpose matter just as much as economic statistics.

The good news is that pessimism is not destiny.

The same generation expressing anxiety about the job market is also the most adaptive, technologically fluent, and entrepreneurial generation in modern history. Young Americans are already building businesses online, creating entirely new industries, using AI tools creatively, and reshaping what work looks like in real time. Even leaders in the AI sector argue this technological transformation can create enormous opportunity if the country embraces it thoughtfully and prepares people for it.

America has reinvented its economy before. We can do it again. But it will require leaders willing to stop treating every issue as a partisan fight and start treating it as a practical challenge to solve together.

Young Americans do not need empty promises. They need leaders willing to level with them about change, invest in their future, and build an economy where hard work still creates opportunity.

That is the kind of future Forward believes is still possible. **Please forward this to your friends, family, and coworkers. It helps us introduce them to Forward and to what we are building. Also consider inviting them to one of our upcoming events listed below. We'd love to meet them.**

Friend, Voting Rights Fund is an organization dedicated to improving the accessibility and security of voting in this country. In the past, we’ve focused on issues like voter registration, voter ID laws, the repeal of the Voting Rights Act, and new initiatives like the Department of Homeland Security’s registered voter list. We elect champions across the country who stand up and fight against bad initiatives designed to limit voting and disenfranchise Americans. Yet underneath all of these issues, a single factor cuts across:**money in politics.** The state of campaign finance reform is an issue [most Americans agree](http://links.votingrightsfund.org/s/c/j9qR86RSY4hYG-2vn5l13vfXaALMbErgl3w-89VlCN2Gfz-FHqNVsVCADSMqxjfKmr4zC-UaWQJ30e5aP9lMryrzXpAm75-tRrQQhfJZFo1BP5OmjaSvCF7jgOaN-i_BoXVdaNDyhhsHD6zzhztePy_0uYmG1bEQG1QZHw9ksseRAwyxuPNWt2aqNXLGeQXFir_JWIy_8faZFsmIwfCYTqapQ1RQelC2jSTCnL3XPlh0FlX8OlLAXh0P33xpE1zBvlVZ-dEs9y9HXI4VS0OWd7c94n09lkLoOkwadRGapXSA_1YUN_cM-xAAs6v7fETJwSGQNAYTm-ptRAtuZ0LATOF1Y8Yb2E4HRTbfWi8rixgIw_ZOC1sDX1S-BxDY5fPhk_jnJF6hseU7tPLO3-yxNgVhd09Y9AKVUrOuTIpo7PjbCvmgur0ET-BwwTK6hMK2W_11cVOZb9jbzYx96t1XFSFjURaEyAPz9Y-5wK2gtN51uqRxvTD_J62eskNDrY3GkDpK-Ai-0EHI0HG7ChcipknGeLjbUXlvjcUGqCf-cK7Cd-rnsSR0ErI/fj_ZgW-bqwQutq9nw6Cc3XDSMdchG872/20) is in desperate need of change. Each presidential campaign becomes the new most expensive election in history, costing an estimated $24 billion in 2024. This inflation in our politics has had two simultaneous effects: a trickle-down increase on congressional and even local politics, and the sustainment of the political money ecosystem. Over a dozen House races in 2024 had a price tag above $25 million. **When politics becomes too expensive for ordinary people to run, it pushes average Americans out and invites billionaires to take over.** We published a graph last year showing the proliferation of spam and scam PACs in the voting rights space. It’s no secret that PACs have been a massive contributor to the importance of money in politics, but structural changes to our laws opened the door for these bad actors. [](http://links.votingrightsfund.org/s/c/STbZI6Wail7lpTmhd-AQceyjUPPfQ5t_9SGGZDhRLXsHa3VYwbFi2NlFXOX4w7FuXNnJnR6vchYDbaKLFRlboN6xmY3h4Q00d9kgyMjbtrysfYRQxPWQWzMboQWLyuAX7ljC2bF-kxpZ6pHpPBe5HymvQTZ4QRvgUm-dFLVypKkwi-2hY8OYJkNy3G4wsJ_wNcbKfw-1D_SSJfzsejdEP0lsSjjgxYMvPqj2sYlBhStRJ2w0lCUvS4aGOqmtpo8vJ_vcbHG0EShq9Fatwl_Y-z4twjex0QwfYz_E7w2aSKiPwdyEUq5-m4_s6QUHQzAHHvyxKX0H29HyhWZxmY_3gYHOm859bOFK853cQlXwDk7LU1odHdMf4jCOQALDvKs0-6e7cPwFUAop6lXBGVQ693lvycjpTh6JOBbBf9jcGsdJZ9W3G6E8pmYTz58TVVooBlhgwhw0Ih4kfA3XTQsdWwky8mfWCk9aIuceHhaddoG6nernQDq_WT3jPm1T5rcFMdkTcq0zgeq9UOAH6AlXl7PZ0BYhtj-w-ENoqwRA3ell7RgMRWycgWV8r_Q2v4WL3ZgSFVpBC5ORqm_M8Dk7GU_B2iq5qa1US9V-h-ZeSiyQ67Ey2KqckSvsOMx-iZF0ddcTU0nkWEbzZVdpcl5CDiDWuLZ4YfmrbhPzGRZSsDOiIKE3qvzmalQnqXDT0rUs6SH5Z7kLJ-nSsAHruN1qbVfbJxl-cd1ASSNE-cUugUrEKIuYigeulH44Of8WGb8TmUX_YFyfMfp7QTKHROUQRivI18YzlK4AZCcArVTm-mdPWiEQ04ZFJ4ag1izAupdVaHLLvgRfXtUFaofOayfVGpl9YVBolkYmv4mZsouxG5kTT-TFBbNlEIbeP_ksRDULyQWLrFQf4V3ny_At0D2B/rT00U_UF4AJsfo51coSNys4pjBS_PPcD/20) It won’t come as a surprise to many reading this that the _Citizens United_ decision was one of those changes. What might surprise many is that one of the largest, most well-funded PACs in the country is the [End Citizens United PAC](http://links.votingrightsfund.org/s/c/J-AQWVNJ2wkvU4hewaFUEo2i1fKoJHxuEDkbTT5zYnM0Y8guJFU5TtEvGPS11Pyr_CePvlcFSuMM-nWI4iQ8PmznTjSPZRHzMPGMtNattt8xVSea1TlDLYPFU_AIb5PvmnOU3GIK-2REuidiuaqodGuOW_cdnpb1Y92FnG4OAwaj4eDXnZt4ph0leYb6Kc0TwbPwI7HvNvC67A-Z-Z_J8ITLKKyRBIsamL7g-JI7mKPwgGvq8oxxPxICy70JkL9IK5-dhwzHXJUjYl2ojzQTUyPXscJBzxNOEItY7EB8TYCOcHz9IRrWz_ZjCaVFjFgjCDflyOZe0IAGam4cGxnzj7xH4EdnfSeFFBHQh9-ttS7MKI02qEaZJuwqYozhLi16JH4SbgIs6H2b5_jrT2lrsWh8hcxQ-EY/6SgkapkxeOURFtyqKT9OM8QILCRKTha6/20). **Money has become the key lever by which political change is achieved, and its concentration determines everything.** The United States has tried to reform the system many times, including the bipartisan McCain-Feingold bill. Individual states have passed regulations governing dark money and encouraging transparency around political donations.**But it isn’t enough.** No amount of transparency alone will solve this problem. [Donald Trump recently released stock trade disclosures](http://links.votingrightsfund.org/s/c/ftcyQ-uDX6OAIMbA3kKZsGbeyeO5zdxTiK4YCC-Y3gbQbu_P81Etw4qFMvD5W66OBFYpbVTp8HRSvnJLL8HIy4GkB9K_izOpbz1D1rweaW1NBbRe0Zmndt2ljvg7U2W4gYCreKDkujVji6LKizqVidmjqGpiUaCpL1J_gQEAzNITwEjPT-ckC6Ew8j4AGSc57dlczpmroLxSgamJtU_ZUuwyk9cQCOpaNuA87OcxlZWUQwqts76U4pLpxO_aToYQku7Ve-7HjyoOW7ZmaU8tQFSSzTOeYtjxE4CJ6M8ZijBqnApfwIdd4TrawZ5fASqwKtRryQdn6ToPg0HUFiLUpZrBRmPJoWeun8O7JrOgjxDSb85d9D1pLXspCQmDST03n2Veiy_Jc6rj3dn7htCCVSRPgPUHrCZyhtUVHy-iQlZ4VKcU_cmSaVZIoJE1MhEtT3O2qO62Qk4YwE9ldi-4S67zZt0KIrL7IfWpFFpC4FYlP9yQltjvqVNWY0xJkWkqwzXyHZezCBe_1jzsXuKAeZQwbDk7ZsRKZWNWtQj8dseQKzUXJg/u3NdYt5mrQvrWrTxMks8KH-GxpWvQyFR/20) showing he has been more active than any president in history in using stocks for personal gain while in office. While we can see corruption in plain sight, it often feels like no one is willing to stop it. **We need real structural change.** **That’s why VRF is committing today to taking on a bigger goal. We are not only fighting for voting rights, but also against the money that pushes your voice out of politics.** Voting Rights Fund elects champions who will support initiatives defending your right to vote and fight against this dark money system. clean_body: Political campaigns are becoming too expensive for ordinary Americans, and that’s not an accident. | | | Friend, Voting Rights Fund is an organization dedicated to improving the accessibility and security of voting in this country. In the past, we’ve focused on issues like voter registration, voter ID laws, the repeal of the Voting Rights Act, and new initiatives like the Department of Homeland Security’s registered voter list. We elect champions across the country who stand up and fight against bad initiatives designed to limit voting and disenfranchise Americans. Yet underneath all of these issues, a single factor cuts across:money in politics. The state of campaign finance reform is an issue is in desperate need of change. Each presidential campaign becomes the new most expensive election in history, costing an estimated $24 billion in 2024. This inflation in our politics has had two simultaneous effects: a trickle-down increase on congressional and even local politics, and the sustainment of the political money ecosystem. Over a dozen House races in 2024 had a price tag above $25 million. When politics becomes too expensive for ordinary people to run, it pushes average Americans out and invites billionaires to take over. We published a graph last year showing the proliferation of spam and scam PACs in the voting rights space. It’s no secret that PACs have been a massive contributor to the importance of money in politics, but structural changes to our laws opened the door for these bad actors. It won’t come as a surprise to many reading this that the Citizens United decision was one of those changes. What might surprise many is that one of the largest, most well-funded PACs in the country is the . Money has become the key lever by which political change is achieved, and its concentration determines everything. The United States has tried to reform the system many times, including the bipartisan McCain-Feingold bill. Individual states have passed regulations governing dark money and encouraging transparency around political donations.But it isn’t enough. No amount of transparency alone will solve this problem. showing he has been more active than any president in history in using stocks for personal gain while in office. While we can see corruption in plain sight, it often feels like no one is willing to stop it. We need real structural change. That’s why VRF is committing today to taking on a bigger goal. We are not only fighting for voting rights, but also against the money that pushes your voice out of politics. Voting Rights Fund elects champions who will support initiatives defending your right to vote and fight against this dark money system. Unlike many other organizations, we don’t keep a penny for ourselves. A new memo to Congressional Republicans, obtained by The Capitalist, reveals **[new polling](https://substack.com/redirect/118d50bd-9a93-4ced-b5ef-772aa35fcd53?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from the Market Institute and Trump pollster Fabrizio Ward showing that Alzheimer's may be an unexpected political opportunity for GOP candidates in the midterms. The Republican base and swing voters are responding strongly to candidates who support earlier diagnosis and expanded treatment access.
* * *
## MEMORANDUM
## - Congressional Republicans | Chiefs of Staff
**From: The Market Institute
Date: May 19, 2026
Subject: As midterms approach, supermajority of voters back candidates who prioritize Alzheimer's**
Alzheimer's disease has become a deeply personal and politically potent issue for American voters. More than 7 million Americans are living with Alzheimer's, and voters increasingly see the disease as a direct threat to their families, finances, and futures.
New national and swing state polling shows overwhelming support for expanding access to earlier Alzheimer's detection, diagnosis, and FDA-approved treatments by reducing Medicare and private insurance coverage barriers.
For candidates in competitive districts and states, Alzheimer's represents an opportunity to advance a compassionate, common-sense healthcare issue centered on prevention, patient autonomy, and doctor-led care. For Republicans, in particular, championing better access to Alzheimer's tests and treatments offers a way to lead on healthcare - an issue where Democrats have historically earned more trust.
## Bottom Line
● Candidates who prioritize improving Alzheimer's access perform very strongly across party lines and key swing states.
● The strongest voter reactions center on frustration with insurance barriers, delays, and coverage denials preventing patients from accessing care their doctors recommend.
● Voters overwhelmingly support expanding access to FDA-cleared Alzheimer's tests and FDA-approved treatments through Medicare and private insurance.
● Voters respond most strongly to messages emphasizing fairness, patient choice, doctor-led decision making, and keeping insurance coverage aligned with scientific innovation.

## What the Polling Says | National Landscape
Alzheimer's has become both a healthcare and political priority for American voters.
● 94% agree caregiving creates enormous emotional and financial strain on families.
● 92% agree that earlier detection and treatment can save families emotionally and financially.
● 87% of voters say Alzheimer's is a serious problem in the United States today.
● 87% say fighting Alzheimer's should be a national priority.
● 70% are concerned that they or someone they love could eventually be diagnosed
● 58% report having family members or friends affected by the disease.
Recent focus groups, conducted in Columbus, Ohio, reinforce that voters increasingly view Alzheimer's as an issue touching nearly every American family:
"Chances are very good that either you or a close family member is going to be diagnosed with Alzheimer's. Are you going to act now, or wait until it happens to you?" -- Joy, Republican
"Autonomy is the most important thing, and the more time you can give somebody to be autonomous, that is priceless." -- Kathy, Democrat
## What the Polling Says | Access and Insurance Barriers
The central voter concern is no longer whether treatments exist -- it is whether patients can access them.
● 89% are concerned insurance delays and denials are restricting access to FDA-approved Alzheimer's treatments.
● 89% are concerned doctors avoid prescribing tests or treatments because insurance will not cover them.
● 89% are concerned seniors can only access care if they can afford to pay out of pocket.
Focus group participants repeatedly described insurance companies as obstacles standing between patients and care:
"There's just so many hoops to jump through. The decline sometimes happens before you can get adequate care." -- Laura, Republican
"[Insurance companies] just want to wear you down... so you just give up." -- Kathy, Democrat
"Why would you have an insurance company make a decision like that, sitting right in front of you. ... The doctor should be the one to make that decision." -- Carl, Democrat

* * *
## Policy Support
Support for policies that expand Alzheimer's access is overwhelming nationally and across key swing states.
**●** **92% support the Alzheimer 's Screening and Prevention Act (ASAP Act).**
**●** **90% support expanded Medicare coverage for FDA-cleared blood tests and FDA-approved treatments.**
**●** **89% support greater state-level access to Alzheimer 's blood tests.**
**●** **87% requiring state-regulated plans to cover tests and treatments.**
Support is overwhelmingly bipartisan:
● 90% of Republicans support the ASAP Act.
● 86% of Republicans support expanded Medicare coverage for tests and treatments.
● 95% of Democrats support expanded access measures.
● Swing-state support consistently remains above 85% across policy proposals.
## Political Impact
Candidates who prioritize improving Alzheimer's access gain a substantial electoral advantage.
Nationally:
● 79% say they are more likely to support a candidate who prioritizes better access to Alzheimer's detection, diagnosis, and treatment.
● The issue generates a +72 net vote impact nationally.
Swing state impact remains remarkably consistent:
● Florida: +73
● North Carolina: +74
● Ohio: +71
● Pennsylvania: +73
Focus group participants also indicated that Alzheimer's remains an under-discussed issue politically -- creating an opening for candidates willing to lead:
"If somebody actually said the word Alzheimer's in their platform to get elected, people would notice because it's different." -- Denise, Republican

## Winning Messages
Top-performing messages include:
● Doctors -- not insurance companies -- should decide which tests and treatments are best for patients.
● Patients with Alzheimer's should have access to innovative medicines just like patients with other serious diseases.
● Insurance coverage should keep pace with scientific advances and FDA-approved innovations.
● Earlier detection and treatment can preserve independence, extend time with loved ones, and reduce long-term care costs.
Voters overwhelmingly reject the argument that the country should avoid expanding access because treatments are expensive or not curative. By a margin of 78% to 10%, voters say Americans deserve access to promising Alzheimer's treatments now.
"You can spend a little bit now, or you're gonna pay a whole lot later." -- Kathy, Democrat
## Strategic Implications
1. **Lead with access and fairness**. Voters respond strongly to the idea that patients should not face insurance barriers when FDA-cleared tests and FDA-approved treatments exist.
2. **Emphasize doctor-led care**. The message that physicians -- not insurance companies -- should determine treatment decisions performs exceptionally well across party lines.
3. **Focus on emotional and financial burdens**. Alzheimer's caregiving strain is nearly universal. Voters strongly connect earlier intervention with preserving independence and reducing family hardship.
4. **Treat Alzheimer 's as both a healthcare and cost issue**. Voters strongly believe earlier diagnosis and treatment can reduce long-term care costs and save taxpayer dollars over time.

## Action Grid
● Arm members and surrogates with polling toplines and district/state-specific data.
● Prioritize earned media and local press around patient access stories and insurance barriers.
● Highlight physician and caregiver voices describing delays, denials, and administrative hurdles.
● Emphasize bipartisan voter support and the broad personal impact of Alzheimer's.
● Localize messaging in swing states and districts where caregiving and aging concerns are especially salient.
_Source materials: Fabrizio Ward Alzheimer 's National & State Voter Survey, Apr. 19-23, 2026; Narrative Strategies Focus Groups, Columbus, OH, Apr. 23 & 29, 2026._

Alzheimer's policy may be an unexpected political opportunity for GOP candidates in the midterms. | | | May 21| | | ∙| | Guest post ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Support The Capitalist by getting the SubStack App A new memo to Congressional Republicans, obtained by The Capitalist, reveals from the Market Institute and Trump pollster Fabrizio Ward showing that Alzheimer's may be an unexpected political opportunity for GOP candidates in the midterms. The Republican base and swing voters are responding strongly to candidates who support earlier diagnosis and expanded treatment access. MEMORANDUM - Congressional Republicans | Chiefs of Staff From: The Market Institute Date: May 19, 2026 Subject: As midterms approach, supermajority of voters back candidates who prioritize Alzheimer's Alzheimer's disease has become a deeply personal and politically potent issue for American voters. More than 7 million Americans are living with Alzheimer's, and voters increasingly see the disease as a direct threat to their families, finances, and futures. New national and swing state polling shows overwhelming support for expanding access to earlier Alzheimer's detection, diagnosis, and FDA-approved treatments by reducing Medicare and private insurance coverage barriers. For candidates in competitive districts and states, Alzheimer's represents an opportunity to advance a compassionate, common-sense healthcare issue centered on prevention, patient autonomy, and doctor-led care. For Republicans, in particular, championing better access to Alzheimer's tests and treatments offers a way to lead on healthcare - an issue where Democrats have historically earned more trust. Bottom Line ● Candidates who prioritize improving Alzheimer's access perform very strongly across party lines and key swing states. ● The strongest voter reactions center on frustration with insurance barriers, delays, and coverage denials preventing patients from accessing care their doctors recommend. ● Voters overwhelmingly support expanding access to FDA-cleared Alzheimer's tests and FDA-approved treatments through Medicare and private insurance. ● Voters respond most strongly to messages emphasizing fairness, patient choice, doctor-led decision making, and keeping insurance coverage aligned with scientific innovation. Sponsored by | | ---|---|--- What the Polling Says | National Landscape Alzheimer's has become both a healthcare and political priority for American voters. ● 94% agree caregiving creates enormous emotional and financial strain on families. ● 92% agree that earlier detection and treatment can save families emotionally and financially. ● 87% of voters say Alzheimer's is a serious problem in the United States today. ● 87% say fighting Alzheimer's should be a national priority. ● 70% are concerned that they or someone they love could eventually be diagnosed ● 58% report having family members or friends affected by the disease. Recent focus groups, conducted in Columbus, Ohio, reinforce that voters increasingly view Alzheimer's as an issue touching nearly every American family: "Chances are very good that either you or a close family member is going to be diagnosed with Alzheimer's. Are you going to act now, or wait until it happens to you?" -- Joy, Republican "Autonomy is the most important thing, and the more time you can give somebody to be autonomous, that is priceless." -- Kathy, Democrat What the Polling Says | Access and Insurance Barriers The central voter concern is no longer whether treatments exist -- it is whether patients can access them. ● 89% are concerned insurance delays and denials are restricting access to FDA-approved Alzheimer's treatments. ● 89% are concerned doctors avoid prescribing tests or treatments because insurance will not cover them. ● 89% are concerned seniors can only access care if they can afford to pay out of pocket. Focus group participants repeatedly described insurance companies as obstacles standing between patients and care: "There's just so many hoops to jump through. The decline sometimes happens before you can get adequate care." -- Laura, Republican "[Insurance companies] just want to wear you down... so you just give up." -- Kathy, Democrat "Why would you have an insurance company make a decision like that, sitting right in front of you. ... The doctor should be the one to make that decision." -- Carl, Democrat The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you! Policy Support Support for policies that expand Alzheimer's access is overwhelming nationally and across key swing states. ● 92% support the Alzheimer 's Screening and Prevention Act (ASAP Act). ● 90% support expanded Medicare coverage for FDA-cleared blood tests and FDA-approved treatments. ● 89% support greater state-level access to Alzheimer 's blood tests. ● 87% requiring state-regulated plans to cover tests and treatments. Support is overwhelmingly bipartisan: ● 90% of Republicans support the ASAP Act. ● 86% of Republicans support expanded Medicare coverage for tests and treatments. ● 95% of Democrats support expanded access measures. ● Swing-state support consistently remains above 85% across policy proposals. Political Impact Candidates who prioritize improving Alzheimer's access gain a substantial electoral advantage. Nationally: ● 79% say they are more likely to support a candidate who prioritizes better access to Alzheimer's detection, diagnosis, and treatment. ● The issue generates a +72 net vote impact nationally. Swing state impact remains remarkably consistent: ● Florida: +73 ● North Carolina: +74 ● Ohio: +71 ● Pennsylvania: +73 Focus group participants also indicated that Alzheimer's remains an under-discussed issue politically -- creating an opening for candidates willing to lead: "If somebody actually said the word Alzheimer's in their platform to get elected, people would notice because it's different." -- Denise, Republican Help us defeat the mainstream media, promote capitalism and American exceptionalism. Winning Messages Top-performing messages include: ● Doctors -- not insurance companies -- should decide which tests and treatments are best for patients. ● Patients with Alzheimer's should have access to innovative medicines just like patients with other serious diseases. ● Insurance coverage should keep pace with scientific advances and FDA-approved innovations. ● Earlier detection and treatment can preserve independence, extend time with loved ones, and reduce long-term care costs. Voters overwhelmingly reject the argument that the country should avoid expanding access because treatments are expensive or not curative. By a margin of 78% to 10%, voters say Americans deserve access to promising Alzheimer's treatments now. "You can spend a little bit now, or you're gonna pay a whole lot later." -- Kathy, Democrat Strategic Implications 1. Lead with access and fairness. Voters respond strongly to the idea that patients should not face insurance barriers when FDA-cleared tests and FDA-approved treatments exist. 2. Emphasize doctor-led care. The message that physicians -- not insurance companies -- should determine treatment decisions performs exceptionally well across party lines. 3. Focus on emotional and financial burdens. Alzheimer's caregiving strain is nearly universal. Voters strongly connect earlier intervention with preserving independence and reducing family hardship. 4. Treat Alzheimer 's as both a healthcare and cost issue. Voters strongly believe earlier diagnosis and treatment can reduce long-term care costs and save taxpayer dollars over time. Action Grid ● Arm members and surrogates with polling toplines and district/state-specific data. ● Prioritize earned media and local press around patient access stories and insurance barriers. ● Highlight physician and caregiver voices describing delays, denials, and administrative hurdles. ● Emphasize bipartisan voter support and the broad personal impact of Alzheimer's. ● Localize messaging in swing states and districts where caregiving and aging concerns are especially salient. Source materials: Fabrizio Ward Alzheimer 's National & State Voter Survey, Apr. 19-23, 2026; Narrative Strategies Focus Groups, Columbus, OH, Apr. 23 & 29, 2026. name: David Hogg
subject: DNC Chair Ken Martin should resign
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
We don’t need an autopsy report to tell us what’s wrong with Dems.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260521-1&t=1&akid=3508%2E587540%2EIlGXAc)
Peter, this is absolutely ridiculous.
**[If you’re as pissed off as I am about the DNC autopsy, please pitch in now to help us build a Democratic Party that will meet this moment, not fold when it matters most.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260521_1_dnc.D6ndAH&refcode=em20260521-3508&amount=5&t=2&akid=3508%2E587540%2EIlGXAc)**
Ken Martin ran for DNC chair on releasing the report, then said it wouldn’t be released, and now — after months of pressure — the DNC finally released its 2024 autopsy report. Let’s talk about what is in the report, and perhaps more importantly, what is __not.__
The first thing I did when I downloaded the report was hit Command + F and search for some things that SHOULD be in it if Democrats are serious about learning from our mistakes:
* **Inflation:** 18 results, every single one about talking about adjusting for inflation for presidential fundraising. Not one mention of how inflation impacted people’s lives and votes.

* **Gaza:** 0 results

* **Biden’s Age:** 0 results

Then I scrolled down to the Conclusion section. I’m not even kidding you, it literally says _**“this section was not provided by the author.”**_
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260521_1_dnc.D6ndAH&refcode=em20260521-3508&amount=5&t=3&akid=3508%2E587540%2EIlGXAc)
In another part of the report, it says the problem wasn’t “Democratic policy or party brand.” This is an absolutely wild take from a Party refusing to live in reality.
I don’t know how else to say this: **Our Party brand is _EVERYTHING._ And our candidates _ARE_ our brand.** If our Party cannot come together and show voters that we are the people fighting for the little guy and fighting against the special interests, then we don’t have much of a future as a Party. Democrats need to stand for something, not object to everything.
**We didn’t need an autopsy to tell us the Democratic Party doesn’t know what they’re doing right now.** What we need is real leadership at the DNC.
When Ken was first elected, I encouraged Party members and donors to give him a chance – the job is hard and he should be granted time to get his feet under him. We are supposed to be working towards the same goal of building strong institutions, but he had other plans. And now it has become clear:
**_Ken Martin should resign immediately_** , and the DNC should select a new leader who demonstrates genuine competence, creativity, moral clarity, and a relentless commitment to actually fixing the Democratic Party’s broken brand.
Leaders We Deserve is doing the work to fight for a better Democratic Party by supporting bold, young progressives who are ready to take the reins in the fight for our future — and who won’t put their heads in the sand and ignore the issues Americans care about.
Since I was forced out of the DNC, we at Leaders We Deserve have:
* Endorsed nearly 40 candidates this cycle, going **undefeated** in state legislative races
* Invested $300k into Zohran’s primary election in June 2025, making us the largest investor in his primary campaign
* Elected our first Member of Congress, Christian Menefee, after the passing of two Democratic Representatives in a row left the seat vacant for nearly a year
* Inspired the movement to push for a better Democratic Party by primarying weak, out-of-touch incumbents in safe blue seats

If you believe in a Democratic Party that actually stands for something besides not being Donald Trump, actually listens to the voters over the same old pundits, and stands up to special interests at every level of government — **this is the moment to support our movement.** Let’s show the DNC that we aren’t messing around.
**[Peter, will you contribute $5 to help us build a better Democratic Party?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260521_1_dnc.D6ndAH&refcode=em20260521-3508&amount=5&t=4&akid=3508%2E587540%2EIlGXAc)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260521_1_dnc.D6ndAH&amount=5&refcode=em20260521-3508&t=23&akid=3508%2E587540%2EIlGXAc)**
Thank you for your support — and for believing in the future we’re fighting for.
More soon,
David Hogg

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Add your name if you agree: The president should not be able to own and trade stocks. Or the vice president. Or members of Congress.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2911%2E4032634%2EdeJBac)
---
I’m so sick of Donald Trump’s corruption. I want to be focused entirely on the things that I know matter most to you: Lower prescription drug prices, better wages, and an economy that works for working people. But it seems like every single day Trump is coming up with a new way to use the presidency to enrich himself rather than lower costs for you — and we need to call it out and fight back. Between the frenzy of his $10 billion lawsuit against his own IRS, and the sham settlement that created a $1.8 billion slush fund to compensate January 6th insurrectionists, it was also reported that Trump has been astonishing Wall Street insiders with his trading activity. In just the first three months of this year, Trump’s accounts made over 3,000 stock trades — roughly 60 trades every day the market was open. He traded up to $680,000 in Eli Lilly while his administration shaped policies that could boost the company’s profits from its weight-loss drug. He traded Nvidia — then approved the sale of advanced chips to China. He bought stock in defense contractors like Lockheed Martin, General Dynamics, and Northrop Grumman — while the U.S. is in yet another war in the Middle East. Trump is trading stocks in companies his administration impacts through policy. He's holding the stocks and pulling the levers that determine their value. Looks like corruption. Plain and simple. [**Bottom line: The president should not be able to own and trade stocks. Or the vice president. Or members of Congress. And we have a plan to ban this. If you believe presidents and politicians shouldn’t be allowed to own or trade stocks, add your name now.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-trump-stocks/?source=EW_EMZ31K_COR_ENG_20260521_F&t=8&akid=2911%2E4032634%2EdeJBac) | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-trump-stocks/?source=EW_EMZ31K_COR_ENG_20260521_F&t=9&akid=2911%2E4032634%2EdeJBac)
---
Every modern president before Trump has understood that holding individual stocks while running the country was a fundamental conflict of interest.
But truthfully, this isn't just a Trump problem.
Members of Congress have been doing a version of this for years.
Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are trading stocks in the very industries they regulate and the defense contractors they fund. Making suspicious trades right before major announcements. And facing little to no consequences.
I couldn’t think of a simpler way to restore the people’s trust in their government than banning stock trading by top government officials.
[**Let’s show that this plan has strong, public support: If you agree that presidents, vice presidents, and members of Congress should be banned from owning and trading stocks, add your name here.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-trump-stocks/?source=EW_EMZ31K_COR_ENG_20260521_F&t=10&akid=2911%2E4032634%2EdeJBac)
Working families deserve a government focused on lowering costs and improving lives — not politicians treating public office like a personal investment strategy.
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

Friends, this is important:
The right to vote is foundational to our democracy. It defines our nation and state, and is the reservoir from which all other rights flow.
Here in California, voting in our primary elections is well underway, so I wanted to make sure you know all the ways you can cast your ballot.
Election Day is Tuesday, June 2, but that isn’t the only day you can vote — it’s just the *last* day. Every day between now and June 2 can be Election Day for Californians.
Every Californian should have already received their ballot in the mail, and I encourage you to vote early in any of these secure and reliable ways:
* By mail — fill out and return your ballot via USPS. Put it in the mail it as soon as you’ve filled it out — at least a week before Election Day to avoid delays.
* By dropbox — fill out and return your ballot in one of the hundreds of ballot dropboxes throughout our communities, including at all public libraries. Click here to find a dropbox [https://caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov/] .
* In person — early vote centers will open in 29 counties starting May 30. Find one near you by clicking here [https://caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov/] .
Voting early ensures your ballot is received and counted in plenty of time — but of course, you can also vote in person on Tuesday, June 2.
However you vote — make sure you do it! Your vote is your voice.
For more voting information, including all the ways you can go vote and how to track your ballot, click here. [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/]
Thanks for reading,
Rob
Rob Bonta
Attorney General of California

body:
New Fran profile just dropped
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260521-2834)
Peter,
Journalist Dan Shafer over at [The Recombobulation Area](https://act.francescahong.com/go/13322?t=1&akid=2834%2E105371%2EdV_A2F) just published an in-depth report on this campaign, and we just had to share it with you.
His takeaway? Fran has officially gone from wildcard to contender.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/13323?t=2&akid=2834%2E105371%2EdV_A2F)
Key takeaways:
* **Fran is serious about leading this state.** The caricature her opponents try to project isn't the person voters actually meet. Dan found a candidate who is deliberate, substantive, and clear-eyed about governing — with public education, shared revenue, and healthcare at the core.
* **Our strategy is working.** From packed concert fundraisers to quiet library roundtables, this campaign is showing up where others aren't. As Dan put it: "Hong became the candidate everyone seemed to be talking about."
* **We're meeting the moment.** Voters are hungry for something different. Dan writes that this campaign "might be grasping the authenticity that voters are craving" at a time when only 35% of Wisconsinites view the Democratic Party favorably.
* **People power is real.** 5,548 supporters have taken part in a campaign event so far, across 62 of Wisconsin's 72 counties and more than 350 towns, cities, and villages.

"[T]his campaign has earned the right to be taken seriously, and — perhaps more importantly — to be considered on its merits and on the issues and policies it is advocating for, and not simply by the labels or narratives assigned to it," he writes. "This campaign is succeeding in ways others are not."
[**Read the full piece here.**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/13323?t=3&akid=2834%2E105371%2EdV_A2F)

Team Hong

| | | | | |
Peter,

**If you've filled up your tank lately, you already know. Gas prices are through the roof - well over $5 a gallon and still climbing.**

Thanks to extreme party leadership, the global energy market is in chaos, and right here in Eastern Washington, we’re paying the price.

I hear it everywhere I go: farmers who can't afford the diesel to run their equipment. Workers who have no choice but to drain their paycheck to make that commute. Families worrying how much travel will cost as we approach the holiday weekend. 2nd Harvest, the Spokane-based foodbank for foodbanks, sending out an emergency fundraising plea to cover skyrocketing transportation costs.

What does our freshman Congressman have to say about it? He's telling us this crisis _"could be worse,"_ while his buddy Jim Jordan says higher gas prices are just _"part of life."_

What a slap in the face. We deserve better than being told to just accept this and move on.

**If others won’t listen - or won’t act - I will. That’s a promise.**

**That’s why I’m asking today:**[**Will you take a few moments to tell me how rising gas prices and other costs are affecting you and your household?**](https://conroy4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc047fbc65030d4c4bcc44d19&id=46fd8819c5&e=a7b299e420)
